note: Framework 12.9 SETTING-INFO-1: the ONE source of the More info panels and switch-on confirmations in PIM Manager, and of the per-setting pages on invardia.com. Every entry must carry info.what/enabled/disabled/risk/requires/recommended/docUrl; a key without them fails the product test suite.

info.what: Requires a second administrator to approve any Review & Save commit or row deletion that touches privileged access before PIM Manager writes it. The check runs in PIM Manager at the moment you commit; it applies from the next commit after you save.
info.enabled: A commit that PIM Manager classifies as sensitive is refused until a different administrator has approved it on the Approvals page. You cannot approve your own change unless self-approval is switched on (Settings > Approvals & policy). Changes that are not sensitive commit as before.
info.disabled: Sensitive changes commit straight away. They are still classified as sensitive, validated and written to the audit trail, but nobody else has to approve them.
info.risk: With only one administrator, switching it on means no privileged change can be committed at all. Approval requests are raised on the Approvals page, and that page only takes action when 'Approval-gated offboarding + revoke (preview)' is on. If it is off, sensitive commits are blocked and cannot be approved. Being a Pro feature, it also stops applying if the Pro licence lapses. Reversible: switch it off and the next commit goes through.
info.requires: A Pro licence that covers this tenant (switching it on without one is refused). SuperAdmin to change it. At least two administrators with the Admin role, and 'Approval-gated offboarding + revoke (preview)' switched on under Governance preview so approvals can be raised and decided.
info.recommended: Turn it on when at least two people administer PIM Manager and you want separation of duties. Leave it off for a single-administrator tenant.

info.what: Lets the engine look for resources it does not manage yet. At the end of each engine run it lists your Azure subscriptions and management groups (and Power BI workspaces when that integration is on), and the daily discovery jobs read the Entra, Azure, Power BI, Defender XDR and Intune role catalogs. New items are then handled according to your Discovery auto-create policy.
info.enabled: From the next engine run and the next daily discovery jobs, new resources are found and logged. With the default policy ('flag') they are only reported. A type you set to 'pending' is staged for your review, and a type set to 'auto' is queued to be created as a normal change. The discovery decisions and baseline actions in PIM Manager can be used.
info.disabled: The end-of-run sweep and the daily discovery jobs do nothing (each discovery job is recorded as skipped). Nothing is listed or auto-created, and PIM Manager refuses discovery decisions and baseline actions.
info.risk: Low with the default 'flag' policy, which only reads. If a resource type's policy is 'auto', new subscriptions or workspaces get definitions created without anyone reviewing them first. Reversible: switch it off and discovery stops on the next run. Definitions it already created stay until you remove them.
info.requires: A Pro licence (without one the sweep is skipped, and switching it on is refused). SuperAdmin to change it. 'Scheduled jobs' must be on for the daily discovery jobs to run. The engine identity needs Reader on the Azure scopes you want discovered.
info.recommended: Turn it on with the default 'flag' policy so you are told about new subscriptions and roles, and only set types to 'auto' once you trust the naming.

settings.label: Email alerting
settings.default: Off in the catalog; the standard deployment switches it on

info.what: The master switch for every mail PIM Manager and the engine send. It covers alerts, digests, reminders, escalations, the tier report, access-request and review mails, and the mail that delivers a new admin's first sign-in (Temporary Access Pass). The engine and jobs check it on every send, so a change applies to the next mail.
info.enabled: Mail is sent through your configured mail sender to the intended recipients, still subject to Email controls (kill switch, redirect, allowlist). The daily summary, tier report, reminders and escalations jobs run on their schedule.
info.disabled: Every send is skipped without an error. The daily summary, tier report, reminders and escalations jobs are recorded as skipped, and new admin accounts are still created but their first sign-in mail never arrives.
info.risk: Switching it off silently stops security alerts (engine failure, drift, break-glass, expiring access) and onboarding mail, and nothing on screen shows a failure. Reversible: switch it on and the next mail goes out. Mails skipped while it was off are not re-sent.
info.requires: Free (Community) and Pro. SuperAdmin to change it. A working mail sender (Settings > Mail & alerting > Mail sending) and, for scheduled mail, 'Scheduled jobs' switched on.
info.recommended: On. Use Email controls (kill switch or redirect) instead if you only need to hold mail for a while, for example while testing.

info.what: The switch for posting alerts to a Microsoft Teams or generic webhook. PIM Manager posts an alert to the webhook only when this switch is on AND a valid HTTPS webhook URL is saved in the alerting settings. It is on by default, so an existing webhook keeps working after an upgrade.
info.enabled: When on (the default): if a valid webhook URL is configured, PIM Manager posts each alert to it, also when 'Email alerting' is off -- the webhook is its own channel.
info.disabled: When off: no alert is posted to the webhook, even with a URL saved. Alerts still go by email when email alerting is set up; the alert record says the webhook was switched off.
info.risk: Low. Switched off, a Teams channel that watches for failures goes quiet -- make sure email recipients are set. Reversible at any time; the next alert uses the new value.
info.requires: Free (Community) and Pro. SuperAdmin to change it. A webhook URL in the alerting settings.
info.recommended: Leave it on and control the destination with the webhook URL; switch it off to pause the webhook without losing the saved URL.

settings.label: Workload connectors: Intune + Defender XDR
settings.default: Off, but on automatically while Intune, Defender XDR or workload assignment rows exist

info.what: Lets the engine apply your workload role delegation. This covers Intune and Defender XDR role assignments, including Defender custom roles built from a role specification, and the generic workload-connector rows (where Pro connectors also need a licence). If you never set it, it counts as on whenever such assignment rows exist. A value you save always wins.
info.enabled: On the next engine run, the engine creates and updates the Intune and Defender XDR role assignments (and custom Defender roles) your definitions describe, and removes the ones your definitions remove. Rows for Pro connectors run only with a Pro licence.
info.disabled: The Intune, Defender XDR and workload-connector steps are skipped and reported as not checked, so nothing is assigned or removed there. Groups are still created, and each run warns that their workload role is not being assigned.
info.risk: Switching it on lets the engine write role assignments in Intune and Defender XDR, and remove ones your definitions no longer include. Saving it as off on purpose keeps it off even when rows exist. Reversible: switch it off and the engine stops on its next run, but assignments it already made or removed are not undone.
info.requires: Free (Community) for Intune and Defender XDR. SuperAdmin to change it. The engine identity needs DeviceManagementRBAC.ReadWrite.All for Intune and the Defender XDR role management permission for Defender. Each workload's prerequisites must be green before its assignments are applied.
info.recommended: Leave it unset (it follows your data) or on if you delegate Intune or Defender roles. Switch it off only to pause workload changes.

settings.label: Workload connectors: app-role, Azure DevOps, Dataverse, Business Central, Power Platform
settings.default: Off, but on automatically while app-role or workload assignment rows exist

info.what: The switch for the enterprise-app app-role connector. The engine applies app-role assignments from your app-role definitions only when it is on. Azure DevOps, Dataverse, Business Central and Power Platform rows actually run under 'Workload connectors: Intune + Defender XDR' and need the Pro licence this entry names. This switch does not stop them.
info.enabled: On the next engine run, the engine assigns the enterprise-application app roles your definitions describe, and removes the ones they no longer include, if a Pro licence is installed.
info.disabled: The app-role step is skipped and reported as not checked. Azure DevOps, Dataverse, Business Central and Power Platform rows still run if the Intune + Defender XDR switch is on and a Pro licence covers them.
info.risk: Switching it on lets the engine grant and remove app-role assignments on enterprise applications. Switching it off does not pause the other connectors in its label. Use the Intune + Defender XDR switch, or remove the rows, for that. Reversible: the engine stops on its next run, and assignments already made stay.
info.requires: A Pro licence (switching it on without one is refused, and rows are held). SuperAdmin to change it. The engine identity needs AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All and Application.Read.All for app roles.
info.recommended: On when you manage app-role delegation with PIM Manager. Otherwise leave it unset.

info.what: Controls only whether the engine's end-of-run discovery sweep lists your Power BI workspaces. Power BI workspace role rows are applied by the workload connectors (they need this entry's Pro licence, not this switch), and the daily Power BI discovery job follows 'Discovery sweep' only.
info.enabled: With 'Discovery sweep' also on, each engine run ends by listing Power BI workspaces and handling new ones according to your Discovery auto-create policy for Power BI.
info.disabled: The end-of-run sweep skips Power BI. The daily Power BI discovery job and Power BI role rows are not affected by this switch.
info.risk: Low: it mostly reads. If your Power BI auto-create policy is 'auto', new workspaces get definitions created without review. Switching it off does not stop Power BI role changes. Reversible: switch it off and the next run skips Power BI.
info.requires: A Pro licence. SuperAdmin to change it. Depends on 'Discovery sweep'. The engine identity must be allowed to use the Power BI admin APIs in your tenant (the Power BI service admin setting that lets service principals use read-only admin APIs).
info.recommended: On if you want new Power BI workspaces reported. Control Power BI role assignments through their rows instead.

info.what: Turns on the access-request job that runs every minute. It publishes who may request access to the public request portal, takes in submitted requests, decides them (auto-approved or by the department owner, per department), enables the admin account for the approved time, and disables it again when the time is over. It also shows pending requests on the PIM Manager home page.
info.enabled: Within a minute, people listed as eligible can request their disabled admin account enabled from the portal with a one-time PIN. Approved requests enable the account on the engine's next run, and accounts are disabled again when their window ends. The decision mails are sent.
info.disabled: The job does nothing: new portal requests are not picked up, and accounts that an earlier request enabled are not disabled when their window ends.
info.risk: Switching it on lets disabled admin accounts be re-enabled through a public portal, by auto-approval or one owner's approval. Switching it off while windows are open leaves those accounts enabled until you disable them yourself or switch it on again. Reversible either way, but check for open windows before switching it off.
info.requires: A Pro licence (switching it on without one is refused). SuperAdmin to change it. The public RFA portal deployed (RFA settings: request store). 'Scheduled jobs' on. Departments with owners and an RFA mode on the admins who may request.
info.recommended: On only after the RFA portal is deployed and departments are set up. Leave it on while any access window is open.

settings.label: Access request API (REST, for ServiceNow and other systems)

info.what: Accepts access requests that other systems (for example ServiceNow) send to the REST API on the public broker. A caller can ask for an admin account to be enabled, or a group membership, for a set time, and read or cancel the request. Callers use an allow-listed Entra application token or a PIM API key.
info.enabled: On its next run (within a minute), the access-request job takes in API requests and decides them with the same rules as portal requests. Group requests become a time-limited active membership that is removed at the end. SuperAdmins can create API keys.
info.disabled: Requests that arrive through the API are rejected with 'the access request API is not enabled here', and no new API keys can be created. Portal requests are not affected.
info.risk: Switching it on lets an external system, using a key or application you allowed, enable admin accounts and add group memberships for a time. Anyone holding a valid key can request access. Reversible: switch it off and new API requests are rejected on the next run. Requests already granted run until their end time.
info.requires: A Pro licence (switching it on, or creating an API key, without one is refused). SuperAdmin to change it and to manage API keys. Depends on 'Request for authorization (RFA) portal' being on, and on the public broker being deployed.
info.recommended: On only when a system such as ServiceNow will actually call it. Give each caller its own key with the narrowest scope and an end date.

info.what: Opens the Model Context Protocol endpoint on PIM Manager, so an AI assistant or agent signed in with an Entra account can read who has what, pending changes, jobs and problems. It can also stage and commit changes through the same checks as the PIM Manager page. The signed-in person's PIM Manager role decides what it may do. PIM Manager checks the switch on every call, so a change applies at once.
info.enabled: Signed-in assistants can call the endpoint. Every tool call, reads included, is written to the audit trail. Demo viewers stay refused.
info.disabled: Every call to the endpoint is refused with 'the MCP server is switched off'.
info.risk: Switching it on gives an AI assistant the same reach as the person it signs in as. An Admin or SuperAdmin session can stage and commit privileged changes through it, and the data it reads (who holds which privileged access) leaves PIM Manager to the assistant. Reversible: switch it off and calls are refused at once.
info.requires: A Pro licence (switching it on, or calling it, without one is refused). SuperAdmin to change it. The endpoint's Entra sign-in set up for PIM Manager.
info.recommended: Off unless you use an assistant with PIM Manager. If on, use it with accounts that have the lowest PIM Manager role that does the job.

settings.label: MSP downlink / fan-out
settings.default: Off in the catalog; the standard deployment switches it on

info.what: The switch for replication between a managing tenant and its managed tenants. On a managing tenant it gates the publish job (the signed baseline managed tenants read); on a managed tenant it gates the pull job (reading and applying that baseline). It is on by default, so replication that runs today keeps running after an upgrade.
info.enabled: When on (the default): the pull and publish jobs run on the cadence set on the Job schedule page while a Pro licence covers the MSP role.
info.disabled: When switched off: nothing is published on a managing tenant and nothing is pulled on a managed tenant. Each run is recorded as 'held' with the reason on the Job schedule page, and Home says replication is switched off. Nothing already applied is removed.
info.risk: Medium: while it is off, changes on the managing tenant stop reaching the managed tenants (and a managed tenant stops taking them in). Reversible: switch it on; the next scheduled run catches up.
info.requires: A Pro licence covering the managing tenant / managed tenant role (the replication jobs themselves refuse to run without one). SuperAdmin to change it.
info.recommended: Leave it on. Switch it off only to pause replication on purpose; the Job schedule page also lets you pause just the cadence.

settings.label: Request the licence from Invardia automatically

info.what: Runs the licence-request job every 30 minutes. When no valid Pro licence for this tenant is installed, or the installed one ends within 30 days, PIM Manager asks Invardia for its licence. When one is delivered, it checks the file (checksum, signature, Pro, this tenant) and installs it, with no restart.
info.enabled: On the next 30-minute run, if a licence is needed, PIM Manager sends Invardia the product name, version, this tenant's id, an installation id, and the id and end date of the installed licence if there is one. It then polls until Invardia answers, and shows the status under Settings > Licence. A rejection is never re-requested automatically.
info.disabled: Nothing is sent and no licence is fetched. You register licences yourself under Settings > Licence or Get Started > Licence.
info.risk: When on, it contacts invardia.com and sends this tenant's id. A licence that Invardia delivers is installed only after it verifies here, so a bad file cannot be installed. With it off, a licence can run out without anyone renewing it, and Pro features then stop after the grace period. Reversible at any time. A licence already installed stays.
info.requires: Free (Community) and Pro. SuperAdmin to change it. 'Scheduled jobs' must be on. Outbound HTTPS from the environment to invardia.com.
info.recommended: On, so a Pro licence is renewed before it ends. Switch it off only if your environment must not contact Invardia.

info.what: Runs the install-key job every 6 hours. When this install has a Pro licence for this tenant and no Invardia install key yet, it claims one by sending Invardia the licence file and this tenant's id. The key lets the nightly update take signed Pro releases from Invardia, for the ring Invardia has set, when the update job is deployed with Invardia as its source.
info.enabled: On the next 6-hour run, if no key is held, PIM Manager claims one and shows the result under Settings > Licence. Each update is installed only after its signature, release number and archive checksum are checked. A release that asks for a manual step is held. Status telemetry then also travels with this key.
info.disabled: No install key is claimed. This switch does not stop updates for an install that already holds a key and whose update job uses Invardia. That is decided when the update job is deployed.
info.risk: When on, it sends your licence file and tenant id to invardia.com. A refused claim (key already exists, licence refused) is not retried until the licence changes. Reversible: switching it off stops new claims. A key already claimed stays and keeps working.
info.requires: A Pro licence for this tenant (without one nothing is sent). SuperAdmin to change it. 'Scheduled jobs' on. The update job deployed with Invardia as its update source. Outbound HTTPS to invardia.com.
info.recommended: On for Pro installs that take updates from Invardia. It has no effect on a Community install.

info.what: Runs the uplink job every hour. It reports to Invardia which jobs ran and whether they succeeded (one report per job, never one per run), and once a day a heartbeat with version, edition and licence state. Without an install key it is anonymous: no tenant, no server name, no error text, only an error class and rounded counts. With a Pro install key, reports carry the error text with secrets removed.
info.enabled: From the next hourly run, the job reports at most 20 job results per cycle and the daily heartbeat. A failed send never fails anything else and is retried on the next cycle.
info.disabled: Nothing is sent. If it was on before, one opt-out notice is sent once, then nothing more.
info.risk: When on, it sends status data out of your environment to invardia.com. With a Pro install key that includes shortened, redacted error messages. Reversible: switch it off and the next run sends only the one-time opt-out notice.
info.requires: Free (Community) and Pro. SuperAdmin to change it. 'Scheduled jobs' must be on. Outbound HTTPS to Invardia's uplink.
info.recommended: On, so Invardia support can see a failing job before you call. Switch it off if your policy forbids sending operational data out.

info.what: Adds a setup report to the hourly uplink run: once a day and whenever something changes, the state of the critical settings (updater deployed and scheduled, update ring, install key, licence, mail sender, alert recipients, engine permissions, last successful run, backup, update pinned) as ok, missing, wrong or unknown, plus how many engine permissions are expected, missing and extra. The same list drives the health lines on Home.
info.enabled: With a Pro install key, the next uplink run sends the setup report, then one a day and one on every change. Invardia support sees what is missing and can help before you call. Without an install key nothing of this is sent.
info.disabled: No setup report is sent. The hourly job reports and the daily heartbeat are not affected (they have their own switch).
info.risk: When on, it sends the state of your settings (ids, ok / missing / wrong / unknown, counts and the names of missing Graph permissions) to invardia.com. Never names of people or groups, tenant data, error text or secrets. Reversible: switch it off and nothing more is sent.
info.requires: A Pro install key (identified telemetry). 'Send status telemetry to Invardia' on. SuperAdmin to change it. Outbound HTTPS to Invardia's uplink.
info.recommended: On, so Invardia support can see an unfinished setup or a broken updater before it becomes an incident.

settings.label: Scheduled jobs
settings.default: Off in the catalog; the standard deployment switches it on

info.what: The master switch for the scheduler. Every scheduled job checks it before it runs: engine reconcile runs, the change queue, discovery, digests and reminders, access-request handling, licence checks and requests, telemetry, hybrid AD jobs and the rest. It applies from the next scheduler tick.
info.enabled: Jobs run on the cadence shown on the Job schedule page. The engine reconciles your definitions into the tenant, which creates, updates and removes accounts, groups and assignments.
info.disabled: Every scheduled job is recorded as 'skipped' with status ok, and nothing runs. The engine does not reconcile, no reminders or digests are sent, access windows are not ended, and licence requests stop.
info.risk: Switching it on lets the engine write to your tenant on a schedule. Switching it off makes the environment inert while every job still looks green, so missing work (an account not created, an access window not closed) goes unnoticed. Reversible: switch it on and the next tick resumes. Work skipped in between is caught up by the next reconcile.
info.requires: Free (Community) and Pro. SuperAdmin to change it. 'Request the licence from Invardia automatically', 'Pro updates from Invardia' and 'Send status telemetry to Invardia' all depend on it.
info.recommended: On. Switch it off only for a short, deliberate pause, such as while restoring a configuration backup.

info.what: Turns on the action paths of the Approvals page: raising an approval request, deciding it, and running an approved offboarding. When off, the page can be viewed, but PIM Manager refuses those actions. PIM Manager reads the switch on every request, so it applies at once. The page banner updates on the next reload.
info.enabled: An administrator can raise an offboarding or revoke request with a justification. A different administrator approves it, and running it stages the disable and revoke, which the engine applies on its next run (the account is disabled, never deleted). Requests from 'Second-approver on sensitive changes' can be raised and decided too.
info.disabled: Raising, deciding and running approvals are refused. An edit that would disable an admin now (a past disable date, or status Disabled/Removed) is not saved, so you cannot offboard an admin through PIM Manager. Sensitive commits that need a second approver cannot be approved.
info.risk: Switching it on makes approved offboarding possible, which removes admins' access. The always-on guards stay in force either way: the account-disable circuit breaker, break-glass protection, and offboarding never running automatically. Reversible: switch it off and actions are refused at once. Offboardings already applied are not undone.
info.requires: Free (Community) and Pro. SuperAdmin to change it. At least two administrators, unless self-approval is enabled under Settings > Approvals & policy. Needed by 'Second-approver on sensitive changes'.
info.recommended: On once you have two administrators and want offboarding to go through PIM Manager with a second person's approval.

info.what: Turns on the action paths of the Template Rollout page: adding and revoking exemptions, approving a template version, and deploying a template's rows. When off, the page and its conformance view can be read, but PIM Manager refuses those actions. It applies at once, and the banner updates on the next reload. Promoting a template entry to a ring is not covered by this switch.
info.enabled: A SuperAdmin can record exemptions (template entries this tenant deliberately does not follow), approve template versions, and deploy. Deploying writes the template's rows into your workload assignments as a normal commit, and the engine applies them on its next run.
info.disabled: Adding or revoking exemptions, approving templates and deploying are refused, with 'preview -- disabled'. Exemptions already recorded stay in effect.
info.risk: Switching it on allows exemptions that waive template entries for this tenant, and deployments that let the engine create workload role assignments. Reversible: switch it off and new actions are refused. Rows already deployed and exemptions already recorded stay.
info.requires: Free (Community) and Pro. SuperAdmin to change it and to use the actions. 'Workload connectors: Intune + Defender XDR' on for deployed rows to be applied.
info.recommended: Off until you roll out workload templates. Then turn it on so exemptions are recorded and audited, not handled outside PIM Manager.

settings.label: Edition
settings.default: Not set (shows Pro when a valid Pro licence for this tenant is installed, otherwise Core)

info.what: Records the commercial edition of this tenant (Core, Pro, or Pro (Design Partner)), with a grant basis (paid or design partner) and a note. The value is stored, shown and audited. Which Pro features actually work is decided by the installed licence, not by this choice.
info.enabled: When set: the chosen edition and grant basis are shown here and in the edition field of Feature customization. No feature is unlocked or locked by it. A Pro feature still needs a Pro licence that covers this tenant.
info.disabled: When not set: the card shows Pro if a valid Pro licence for this tenant is installed, otherwise Core.
info.risk: Low. Choosing Pro does not grant Pro features, and choosing Core does not take them away, so it can disagree with what the licence allows. Reversible: choose another value and save.
info.requires: Free (Community) and Pro. SuperAdmin to change it. What it unlocks comes from the licence under Settings > Licence.
info.recommended: Leave it unset, or set it to match your licence, so the record matches what you bought.

settings.label: Scenario
settings.default: Single tenant (used when nothing is set)

info.what: Says which deployment shape this install runs as: a single tenant, a managing tenant, or a managed tenant (hosted centrally or locally). The mode badge at the top, the managing-tenant pages, the managed-tenant pull and publish rows on the Job schedule, the MSP licence requirement and the hourly licence check all follow it. PIM Manager applies it at once, and the engine and jobs from their next run.
info.enabled: When set to managing tenant: the managed-tenant registry and replication pages appear, the managed-tenant enrolment job runs (it updates the network rules of the replication store), and a Pro licence becomes mandatory. As a managed tenant, the pull from the managing tenant is listed and also needs a Pro licence.
info.disabled: When not set or set to single tenant: no MSP pages, no MSP jobs and no MSP licence requirement. The engine manages only this tenant.
info.risk: Choosing a managing or managed role without a Pro licence makes the hourly licence check trip a guard, and replication to managed tenants stops. Choosing the wrong role hides or shows replication pages and jobs. If the engine was deployed with a fixed scenario, it keeps that for its own sign-in until redeployed. Reversible: choose the previous scenario and save.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Managing tenant and managed tenant need a Pro licence that covers the MSP role for this tenant. A managed tenant also needs the managing tenant's replication set up.
info.recommended: Leave it at the single-tenant scenario the installer chose, unless you deploy PIM Manager as a managing or managed tenant.

settings.label: Licence
settings.where: Settings > Features & edition > Licence (register: Settings > Licence or Get Started > Licence)

info.what: The signed licence document from Invardia. It is the one thing that decides which Pro features this environment may use, and whether it may run as a managing or managed tenant. You register it by picking or pasting the file. PIM Manager checks the signature before anything is stored. The card shows edition, status, end date, the bound tenant and each Pro feature's state.
info.enabled: When registered: within minutes, the Pro features it covers become available to PIM Manager, the engine and the jobs, with no restart. After its end date, a grace period (normally 30 days) keeps them working with a warning, and after that they stop. A licence must name this tenant.
info.disabled: When no licence is installed: the Free (Community) edition runs. Pro features are refused with a message naming where to get a licence, and managing or managed tenant replication refuses to run.
info.risk: A licence for another tenant, a Community licence or an expired one unlocks nothing. Registering a new licence replaces the installed one, and features the new file does not cover stop. A file that fails the signature check is refused and the installed licence is left alone. Reversible by registering another licence.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to register a licence (every role can read the card). A licence issued by Invardia for this tenant's id. Optionally, 'Request the licence from Invardia automatically' fetches and installs it for you.
info.recommended: Register your Pro licence here as soon as you receive it, and keep the automatic licence request on so it is renewed before it ends.

settings.label: Home / Overview
settings.default: On (always on -- cannot be switched off)

info.what: The Home page -- the landing page of PIM Manager with per-tier counts, gaps, orphans, engine and job status and the "what needs my attention" call-out.
info.enabled: Home is always shown. It is the page PIM Manager opens on, so it is locked on.
info.disabled: Not possible. The checkbox is locked; if a switched-off value ever reaches the store, PIM Manager ignores it, forces Home back on and shows a warning on the Features card.
info.risk: None -- this is a fixed part of the product, shown here only so the list of surfaces is complete.
info.requires: Nothing else. (Changing any feature on this card needs the SuperAdmin role.)
info.recommended: Nothing to decide -- it stays on.

info.what: Shows or hides the Access map page (Access > Access map): the live graph of who can reach what -- admins, groups, nested groups and targets -- where you can also link people into groups and groups into permissions (staged for Review & commit).
info.enabled: Access > Access map is listed in the menu after the next page reload.
info.disabled: After the next page reload the Access map disappears from the menu and the tab strip for everyone. The page is turned off -- also through a direct link. Nothing in your tenant or configuration changes, and the data behind it is shared with other pages, so this is a way to tidy the menu, not a permission control.
info.risk: Low. People lose the visual way to see and link access; existing delegations are untouched. A link that opens the page directly (for example from a mail, /?tab=map) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On -- the map is the quickest way to understand and check your delegation model.

info.what: Shows or hides the bulk change page (Access > Create & change access (bulk)): duplicate a group or delegation to many targets, bulk-attach, move an admin between groups, each with a preview before it is staged.
info.enabled: Access > Create & change access (bulk) is listed in the menu after the next page reload.
info.disabled: After the next page reload the bulk page is hidden from the menu and tab strip. One-at-a-time creation under Create access and the delegation table under Delegations -- all rows still work. Nothing already staged or committed is changed, and the page is turned off also through a direct link; its requests are shared with other pages, so this tidies the menu, not a permission control.
info.risk: Low. Admins who rely on bulk moves or clones must do them one by one. A direct link (/?tab=authoring) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On if your administrators make larger changes; off is fine for a small team that only uses the guided wizards.

info.what: Shows or hides the Pending changes page (Pending changes > Review & commit queue) -- the one queue where every staged change (configuration edits, revokes, TAP re-issues, session revokes) is reviewed with a diff and committed.
info.enabled: Pending changes > Review & commit queue is listed in the menu after the next page reload.
info.disabled: After the next page reload the commit page is hidden from the menu and tab strip. Every other page still lets people STAGE changes, but there is no menu entry left to review and commit them, so staged changes pile up and never reach the engine. The page is turned off also through a direct link; the server itself does not refuse commits made elsewhere.
info.risk: High for day-to-day use: with this off, nobody can commit from the menu, so nothing new you stage is applied to your tenant. A direct link (/?tab=save) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload; staged changes are kept.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On. Switch it off only on a read-only or demonstration environment where nobody should commit.

info.what: Shows or hides the Check for problems page (Pending changes > Check for problems): it checks your configuration for orphans, naming errors, missing owners and stale roles before you commit, each with a suggested fix.
info.enabled: Pending changes > Check for problems is listed in the menu after the next page reload, with its red error count on the tab.
info.disabled: After the next page reload the page is hidden from the menu and tab strip, so people no longer see the list of problems. Only the page is hidden -- the checks PIM Manager runs on its own when you commit are not switched off by this.
info.risk: Medium: problems in your configuration become less visible, so they are found later -- by the engine or by a failed commit. A direct link (/?tab=validate) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On -- it is the cheapest way to catch a mistake before it reaches the tenant.

info.what: Shows or hides the Review current delegations page (Reviews & controls > Review current delegations): who holds an active assignment right now, with revoke of what is not needed (break-glass accounts are protected; large batches need a second approver).
info.enabled: Reviews & controls > Review current delegations is listed in the menu after the next page reload.
info.disabled: After the next page reload the page is hidden from the menu and tab strip. Nothing is revoked or restored by the switch itself, and the page is turned off also through a direct link; revokes started from other pages still work.
info.risk: Medium: your administrators lose the quick way to see and cut live standing access, so access that should be removed stays longer. A direct link (/?tab=revoke) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On -- seeing and revoking live access is part of keeping standing privilege low.

info.what: Shows or hides the Approvals page (Reviews & controls > Approvals): the second-person queue where an offboarding, revoke or sensitive change is raised, approved or denied by a different admin, and executed.
info.enabled: Reviews & controls > Approvals is listed in the menu after the next page reload, with its count of waiting requests. (Whether its live data loads is decided separately under Settings > Governance preview.)
info.disabled: After the next page reload the page is hidden from the menu and tab strip. The approval requirement itself is NOT switched off: changes that need a second approver still wait for one -- they simply cannot be found from the menu. The page is turned off also through a direct link; approvals raised from other pages still work.
info.risk: Medium: requests waiting for approval can sit unnoticed and the changes behind them never run. A mail's "Open in PIM Manager" link (/?tab=approvals) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload; waiting requests are kept.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro. Settings > Governance preview decides whether the page is live or shown as a preview.
info.recommended: On whenever you use second-approver rules, so approvers can find what waits for them.

info.what: Shows or hides the Jobs & status page (Jobs > Jobs & status): each scheduled job's cadence, last result, next run and failures, with Run now and the run history.
info.enabled: Jobs > Jobs & status is listed in the menu after the next page reload.
info.disabled: After the next page reload only the Jobs & status page is hidden. The jobs themselves keep running on schedule -- the switch does not stop the engine. Engine logs & errors and Job schedule are separate pages and stay in the menu.
info.risk: Low to medium: failed runs and Run now are harder to reach, so a failing job may be noticed later. A direct link (/?tab=jobs) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On -- it is where you see that the engine is healthy.

info.what: Shows or hides the Drift page (Reviews & controls > Drift: live vs desired), which compares your tenant with what PIM says it should be, per area. The old Governance page it is named after no longer exists, so today this switch controls only the Drift page.
info.enabled: Reviews & controls > Drift: live vs desired is listed in the menu after the next page reload.
info.disabled: After the next page reload the Drift page is hidden from the menu and tab strip. The scheduled drift check keeps running and its results are still stored -- only the page is hidden. Coverage & gaps, Newly discovered resources and Job schedule are not affected.
info.risk: Medium: drift between your tenant and the desired state becomes harder to see. A direct link (/?tab=drift) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On -- drift is how you find changes made outside PIM.

info.what: Shows or hides the Look up a role page (Access > Look up a role): what a role can do, which roles grant an action (least privilege first), who can activate a role, and a side-by-side compare of two roles.
info.enabled: Access > Look up a role is listed in the menu after the next page reload.
info.disabled: After the next page reload the page is hidden from the menu and tab strip. It is turned off also through a direct link, and the server refuses its own requests while it is off. It is read-only, so nothing in your tenant or configuration changes.
info.risk: Low: people lose a read-only research tool. A direct link (/?tab=roleperms) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On -- it helps pick the least-privileged role before you delegate.

settings.label: Audit
settings.default: On (always on -- cannot be switched off)

info.what: The Audit trail page (Operations > Audit trail): every change, who made it and when, with before and after, filter, search and export.
info.enabled: The audit trail is always shown, so the record of who changed what can always be reached.
info.disabled: Not possible. The checkbox is locked; a switched-off value in the store is ignored, the page is forced back on and a warning is shown on the Features card.
info.risk: None -- the audit trail is deliberately not something you can hide.
info.requires: Nothing else. (Changing any feature on this card needs the SuperAdmin role.)
info.recommended: Nothing to decide -- it stays on.

info.what: Shows or hides the Support page (Operations > Support): a one-click connectivity and permission self-check (SQL, Graph, Azure) and a sanitized diagnostics bundle to hand over when you need help.
info.enabled: Operations > Support is listed in the menu after the next page reload.
info.disabled: After the next page reload the page is hidden from the menu and tab strip. It is turned off also through a direct link, and the server refuses its own requests while it is off. Nothing is sent or changed by the switch.
info.risk: Low: when something breaks, the self-check and the diagnostics bundle are harder to find, so troubleshooting takes longer. A direct link (/?tab=support) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On -- it is the first place to look when a permission or connection is missing.

settings.label: Settings
settings.default: On (always on -- cannot be switched off)

info.what: The Settings page itself -- where this Features card lives.
info.enabled: Settings is always shown, so you can never lock yourself out of the place where features are switched back on.
info.disabled: Not possible. The checkbox is locked; a switched-off value in the store is ignored and Settings is forced back on.
info.risk: None -- locked on by design.
info.requires: Nothing else. (Changing any feature on this card needs the SuperAdmin role.)
info.recommended: Nothing to decide -- it stays on.

info.what: Shows or hides the guided wizards (Access > Create access): create an administrator (with a future creation date and TAP start), build a direct group, or delegate a permission -- names, level, tier and plane are derived for you.
info.enabled: Access > Create access is listed in the menu after the next page reload.
info.disabled: After the next page reload the wizards are hidden from the menu and tab strip. New admins and delegations can then only be made through the bulk page or the delegation table. Nothing existing changes, and the page is turned off also through a direct link.
info.risk: Low to medium: without the guided path, people build access by hand and naming or placement mistakes become more likely. A direct link (/?tab=new) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On -- the wizard is the safest way to create admins and delegations.

info.what: Shows or hides the Invite a guest or consultant page (Admin accounts > Invite a guest or consultant): B2B guest invitation into the delegation model, and enable or disable a managed consultant account.
info.enabled: Admin accounts > Invite a guest or consultant is listed in the menu after the next page reload.
info.disabled: After the next page reload the page is hidden from the menu and tab strip. Guests and consultants that already exist keep their access, and the engine keeps applying their end dates. The page is turned off also through a direct link.
info.risk: Low: inviting a guest or switching a consultant account on or off from the GUI becomes harder. A direct link (/?tab=onboarding) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On if you work with external admins or consultants; off is fine in a tenant with only internal admins.

info.what: Shows or hides the editable tables: Access > Delegations -- all rows (change an eligibility from 90 to 365 days, Active or Eligible, or the policy of an existing delegation) and Access > All records (the raw records behind every page).
info.enabled: Both table entries are listed under Access after the next page reload.
info.disabled: After the next page reload both table entries are hidden from the menu and tab strip. Existing delegations are untouched, but there is then no menu path to edit an existing delegation's duration, assignment type or policy in bulk. The table is turned off also through a direct link.
info.risk: Medium for operations: routine changes to existing delegations get harder. A direct link (/?tab=grid) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On -- it is the quickest way to change existing delegations.

info.what: Shows or hides the Reports page (Reviews & controls > Reports): "who can do what" and the reverse -- pick a person to see everything they can reach, or a role to see who can activate it; printable and exportable evidence for an auditor.
info.enabled: Reviews & controls > Reports is listed in the menu after the next page reload.
info.disabled: After the next page reload the page is hidden from the menu and tab strip. Reports are read-only, so nothing changes in your tenant.
info.risk: Low: audit evidence is harder to produce from the GUI. A direct link (/?tab=reports) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it on and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On -- auditors and owners use it to confirm who can do what.

info.what: Shows or hides the Access reviews page (Reviews & controls > Access reviews): recertification campaigns end to end -- attest (approve, deny, recertify) with a justification, assign reviewers, send reminders and export the evidence.
info.enabled: Reviews & controls > Access reviews is listed in the menu after the next page reload. Turning the page on does not start a campaign by itself.
info.disabled: The page is hidden from the menu and tab strip. Campaigns and results already stored are kept. A direct link shows "this page is turned off", and the server refuses the page's own requests while it is off. In the Free (Community) edition the entry is always listed, marked PRO, whatever this switch says, and opens the Free vs Pro page.
info.risk: Low: switching it on only adds a page. Switched off, open campaigns are harder for reviewers to reach (a direct link /?tab=accessreview shows "this page is turned off" instead). Reversible: switch it back and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Running campaigns is a Pro feature.
info.recommended: On when you run recertification campaigns (Pro); otherwise leave it off.

info.what: Shows or hides the Tenant Baseline page (Templates > Tenant Baseline): how this tenant, and every tenant you manage, compares with the approved templates, and rolling a template version out by ring.
info.enabled: Templates > Tenant Baseline is listed in the menu after the next page reload. Whether the page loads live data and actions is decided separately under Settings > Governance preview, which is off by default.
info.disabled: The page is hidden from the menu and tab strip. Nothing is rolled out or rolled back by the switch. A direct link shows "this page is turned off", and the server refuses the page's own requests while it is off.
info.risk: Low: switching it on only adds a page; any rollout still has to be started on purpose. A direct link (/?tab=conformance) shows "this page is turned off" instead. Reversible: switch it back and reload.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. Settings > Governance preview must also be on for the page to be live. Most useful on a managing tenant.
info.recommended: Off on a single tenant; on for a managing tenant that rolls templates out to managed tenants.

settings.label: MSP Downlink
settings.default: On on a managing tenant; locked off everywhere else

info.what: Shows or hides the Managed tenants page (Reviews & controls > Managed tenants): which of your central admins and roles reach each managed tenant, what was held back and why, and the per-relationship projection policy. It exists only on a managing tenant.
info.enabled: On a managing tenant, Reviews & controls > Managed tenants is listed in the menu after the next page reload.
info.disabled: The Managed tenants page is turned off (also through a direct link) and the server refuses its own requests while it is off. Replication itself is not stopped by this switch, and the Managed tenant registry and Replication overview pages stay visible. On a single tenant or a managed tenant the checkbox is locked off with the reason, and an on value is never saved. In the Free (Community) edition the page is listed as PRO.
info.risk: Low: it hides or shows a page only. With it off, a managing tenant loses its view of what reaches each managed tenant and what was held back. Reversible: switch it on and reload.
info.requires: A managing tenant (this tenant must manage other tenants). Managing and managed tenants are a Pro feature. SuperAdmin role to change.
info.recommended: On for every managing tenant -- it is where you check that your central admins reach the right managed tenants.

settings.label: Environment name
settings.where: Settings > Naming & accounts > Environment name (also Get Started > Environment name)
settings.default: Blank (no name shown; mails use the tenant name)

info.what: A short name for this PIM environment, at most 40 characters -- for example Test (EU) or Production -- so several open PIM Managers, and their mails, can be told apart.
info.enabled: When set: the name shows at the top of every page (Environment, left of Mode) right after saving and in the browser tab as "PIM Manager (<name>)". Every mail PIM sends starts its subject with [<name>] and carries it in the footer, and the PIM Activator commands on Client onboarding use it as the environment's name. The engine picks it up on its next run.
info.disabled: When blank: no name is shown in the header or the browser tab, and mails fall back to the tenant name (or the tenant id). The Activator commands use "PIM". The Get Started step stays open until a name is set.
info.risk: Cosmetic, nothing is changed in your tenant -- but a wrong name (Production on a test tenant) misleads people about where they are acting. It is never copied to another environment by Copy settings or a backup restore. Reversible: change or clear it at any time.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change; every signed-in role can read it. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: Set it on every environment, e.g. Production and Test (EU), so nobody acts in the wrong one by mistake.

settings.label: Admin account domain
settings.where: Settings > Naming & accounts > Admin account domain

info.what: The domain after the @ in every admin account PIM creates in this tenant, picked from the tenant's verified domains. On a managed tenant it is also the domain the admins replicated from the managing tenant are created at -- the managing tenant's domain is never carried over.
info.enabled: When set: from the next engine run, new admin accounts whose row has no full address are created as <name>@<this domain>, and the admin wizard proposes that domain. Existing accounts keep their address -- nothing is renamed. Only a verified domain can be saved.
info.disabled: When blank: new admins are created at whatever Entra ID marks as the tenant's default domain, read at each engine run (the classic behaviour).
info.risk: Changing it after admins exist: an admin row stored with only a user name is then looked up at the new domain first. PIM remembers the domains used before (every change is recorded), so assignments and offboarding still find an account created at an old domain or the default domain, and offboarding remembers the account by its id once found. Reversible: pick the old value again; accounts created meanwhile keep the new domain.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. PIM Manager needs Domain.Read.All or Organization.Read.All to list the verified domains (without it nothing can be picked). Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: Leave it at the tenant default unless your admins must live on a dedicated admin domain; decide before the first admins are created.

info.what: For a live demo environment. While on, every signed-in member of the demo guest group becomes a demo viewer: they can open every page and stage changes in their own browser, but the server refuses every commit, approval, job run, revoke and settings change they try. Everyone else keeps their own role.
info.enabled: Within about 15 seconds of saving, members of the demo guest group get read-only access to every page at Reader level -- even if they hold no PIM Manager role -- and any role they had above that is capped. If the group cannot be read from Entra ID, nobody is treated as a demo viewer until it can: every signed-in person keeps their own role (a visitor without one sees nothing), a warning is logged and Home shows it. Applies to the hosted PIM Manager only, never the local console.
info.disabled: Off: demo mode is not consulted at all -- no group lookup, every role works as before.
info.risk: It widens who can see: demo group members read every page a Reader can (secrets stay masked). If the group later cannot be read, the visitors lose their access and the administrators keep theirs. Saving is refused if the group cannot be read or you are in it yourself. Reversible: switch it off. A config restore or Copy settings never changes it.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. PIM Manager must be able to read the demo guest group and its members in Entra ID (GroupMember.Read.All or Group.Read.All). Uses Demo guest group. Hosted PIM Manager only.
info.recommended: Off, except on an environment set up purely as a public or customer demo.

settings.label: Demo guest group
settings.default: Blank (uses the built-in default demo group name)

info.what: The Entra ID group, by display name or object id, whose members become demo viewers while Demo mode is on. Nested members count. Guests are matched by their home address as well as their guest UPN.
info.enabled: When set: while Demo mode is on, members of this group (looked up through Entra ID, re-read every 5 minutes) get demo access -- read every page, stage changes, save nothing. A name must match exactly one group. It has no effect while Demo mode is off.
info.disabled: When blank: the built-in default demo group name is used, shown as the placeholder in the field.
info.risk: Choosing a group with real administrators in it caps them to demo access while Demo mode is on; choosing a large group lets all its members read every page. Saving with Demo mode on is refused if the group cannot be read or you are a member yourself. Reversible: change the group or switch Demo mode off.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role to change. PIM Manager must be able to read the group and its members (GroupMember.Read.All or Group.Read.All). Only matters when Demo mode is on.
info.recommended: A dedicated group that holds only demo visitors and none of your administrators.

settings.label: Prefix by admin type
settings.where: Settings > Admin name prefixes & environment suffixes
settings.default: internal-adminuser: none, external-adminuser: x-, external-guest: none

info.what: One prefix per admin type (internal admin, external admin / consultant, guest). The prefix fills the {AdminTypePrefix} token in the admin account patterns, so an external admin can be named x-admin-abc-id while an internal one is admin-abc-id. A prefix may itself contain tokens, e.g. adm-{TenantCommonName}-.
info.enabled: When set: every admin account name generated from now on (Create admin wizard, CSV import, central admin script, on-premises AD names) uses the new prefix for that admin type. PIM Manager also uses the prefixes to recognise admin accounts and to check that admin rows match your convention (a warning, not a block).
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: internal admins and guests get no prefix, external admins get x-. A row that does not name an admin type uses the type set in AdminTypeDefault.
info.risk: Existing accounts are never renamed -- the engine works from the user name stored on each admin row. After a change, older rows can show naming warnings, and recognition of admin accounts widens to include the new prefix. Reversible: put the old value back and save; nothing in your tenant changes.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager to change it. Free (Community). Works together with the admin account patterns (it only appears in a name where a pattern contains {AdminTypePrefix}) and AdminTypeDefault.
info.recommended: Keep the shipped prefixes unless your organisation already has its own convention -- set it once, before you create the first admins, so every account follows one convention.

settings.label: Suffix by environment
settings.where: Settings > Admin name prefixes & environment suffixes

info.what: One suffix per environment: Entra ID (cloud) and on-premises Active Directory. It fills the {Platform} / {EnvironmentSuffix} token in admin and group names, e.g. admin-abc-id for the cloud account and admin-abc-ad for its AD twin.
info.enabled: When set: new admin names use the new suffix. The hybrid worker also uses the two suffixes to pair a cloud admin with its AD account (replace the cloud suffix with the AD suffix) for just-in-time AD group membership, and it only REMOVES AD group members whose name ends with the AD suffix. Group names whose pattern contains {Platform} use the suffix of your default environment.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: -ID for Entra ID and -AD for Active Directory. If a suffix is missing the engine still falls back to -ID / -AD.
info.risk: This is not cosmetic on hybrid tenants: change the suffixes after admins exist and the hybrid worker can stop finding their AD accounts (no JIT AD membership), leave old -AD members standing in AD groups, or start treating other accounts with the new suffix as removable members. Existing account names never change. Reversible: restore the old values; the next hybrid run returns to the old pairing.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community) for naming; the AD pairing applies only with on-premises Active Directory (Pro, hybrid worker). The hybrid Active Directory settings can override the cloud / AD suffix pair.
info.recommended: Keep -ID / -AD. If you must change them, do it before the first admin is created, and never on a tenant whose hybrid worker already manages AD group membership.

settings.label: Direct-group types -- Tag prefix
settings.where: Settings > Group naming values (the role prefix also in Get Started > Naming)
settings.default: role: ROLE-, organisation: ORG-, department: DEPT-, project: PROJ-, crossorg: CORG-

info.what: The start of the tag of each direct-group type (role, organisation, department, project, cross-org). It fills {GroupTypePrefix}; the rest of the tag is {ShortName}, e.g. ROLE-HelpDesk. The tag is then placed in the PIM group pattern to give the group name.
info.enabled: When set: groups created from now on in the Create access wizard get the new tag prefix. PIM Manager also uses the prefixes to tell which type an existing tag belongs to (the access map groups role and organisation groups by prefix, and a cloned group keeps its type).
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: the shipped prefixes are used. A blank prefix cannot be saved -- tags of different types would collide.
info.risk: Existing groups keep their tag and name. After a change, groups with the old prefix are shown under OTHER in the access map and a clone of one is treated as a role group. Reversible: restore the old prefix.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). Nothing else.
info.recommended: Keep the shipped prefixes unless you have an existing tagging scheme; decide before you create your first groups, because a group's name is fixed once it exists.

settings.label: Direct-group types -- Administrative unit
settings.default: role: PIM-ROLES, organisation: PIM-ORGANIZATION, department: PIM-DEPARTMENTS, project: PIM-PROJECTS, crossorg: PIM-CROSSORG

info.what: The administrative unit (by its tag) that a new group of each direct-group type is placed in.
info.enabled: When set: the Create access wizard puts new groups of that type in the named administrative unit. If no administrative unit with that tag is defined yet, the wizard stages one with the group, named by the administrative unit name pattern; the engine creates it on the next run after you commit.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: the shipped administrative units are used (PIM-ROLES, PIM-ORGANIZATION, ...).
info.risk: Only new groups are affected; existing groups stay in their current administrative unit. A new value can create an extra administrative unit in your tenant on the next engine run. Reversible: restore the old value; an administrative unit already created stays until you remove its definition.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). The engine identity needs rights to create administrative units (for example AdministrativeUnit.ReadWrite.All) when a new one is staged.
info.recommended: Keep the defaults so each group type has its own administrative unit and can be delegated separately.

settings.label: Permission-group administrative units
settings.default: L0: PIM-L0, L1: PIM-L1, L2: PIM-L2

info.what: The administrative unit a permission group (an Entra role, Azure role or workload role group) is placed in, by its privilege level L0, L1 or L2.
info.enabled: When set: new permission groups from the permission wizard, coverage suggestions and discovery (Azure, Power BI, Power Platform) get the new administrative unit for their level.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: PIM-L0, PIM-L1 and PIM-L2.
info.risk: Only new definitions are affected; existing permission groups keep their administrative unit. If the named administrative unit is not defined, the new group cannot be placed and the check before commit flags it. Reversible: restore the old value.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). The administrative unit must exist as a definition.
info.recommended: Keep one administrative unit per level, so you can delegate who manages Tier 0 groups separately from the rest.

settings.label: Service names
settings.default: entra: Entra-ID, azure: Azure, powerbi: PowerBI, powerplatform: PowerPlatform, bundle: Bundle

info.what: The first part of a permission-group tag ({Service}), per service, e.g. Entra-ID-UserAdministrator-L1-T0-CP-ID.
info.enabled: When set: new permission groups from the permission wizard and from discovery (Azure, Power BI, Power Platform) and bundles start with your service name.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: the shipped names (Entra-ID, Azure, PowerBI, PowerPlatform, Bundle).
info.risk: Only new tags and names change; existing groups keep theirs. Your estate then has two spellings for one service, which makes filtering and reports harder. Reversible: restore the old value.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). Nothing else.
info.recommended: Keep the defaults unless you need a shorter or translated name; decide before the first permission groups are created.

settings.label: Admin word
settings.where: Settings > Naming conventions > Naming words (also Get Started > Naming)

info.what: The word your admin accounts use, e.g. Admin or adm. It fills {AdminWord} in the admin account patterns (and any other pattern that uses it), so one naming template serves every tenant.
info.enabled: When set: new admin names use the word (adm-abc-id instead of admin-abc-id). PIM Manager also derives the admin-account recognition prefixes from it, and checks admin rows against it.
info.disabled: When blank: Admin. A blank value is saved as Admin.
info.risk: Existing accounts keep their names. Accounts named with the old word are still recognised through the admin account prefixes, but their rows can start showing naming warnings, and a high-privilege account with no Purpose may no longer route to the high-privilege AD OU. Reversible: restore the old word.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). Used only where a pattern contains {AdminWord} (the shipped admin patterns do).
info.recommended: Set it once, before the first admin is created, to the word your organisation already uses.

settings.label: Tenant common name
settings.where: Settings > Naming conventions > Naming words (also Get Started > Naming)

info.what: An optional short name for this tenant, e.g. TST or EU. It fills {TenantCommonName} wherever you use it in a pattern, a prefix or a suffix, so the same naming template works in every tenant.
info.enabled: When set: names generated from now on carry it where your patterns place the token, e.g. admin-tst-abc-id.
info.disabled: When blank: the token disappears and the separator it leaves is removed. The shipped patterns do not use it, so it has no effect until you add {TenantCommonName} to a pattern.
info.risk: Existing names never change. Changing it after admins or groups exist gives you two naming styles in one tenant, and admin-recognition prefixes built from it change with it. Reversible: restore the old value.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). Only matters if a pattern, prefix or suffix contains {TenantCommonName}.
info.recommended: Use it when you run several tenants (test, production, managed tenants) and want each tenant's accounts to be recognisable at a glance; otherwise leave it blank.

settings.label: AdminAccountPattern (admin account name)
settings.where: Settings > Naming conventions (also Get Started > Naming)

info.what: The user name of a normal (day-to-day) admin account. Names are rendered in lower case, and a domain is added from the admin account domain setting.
info.enabled: When set: the Create admin wizard, CSV import and the hybrid worker (for AD rows without a user name) generate new names with it. The literal start of the pattern is also one of the prefixes the engine uses to find admin accounts in your tenant, and admin rows are checked against it (a warning, not a block).
info.disabled: It cannot be saved blank: this is one of the four required naming keys, and the save is refused. A blank value left in the store by an older version makes the engine use the shipped default for it, with a warning in every run, until you set your own.
info.risk: Existing accounts are not renamed; the engine uses the user name stored on each row. A new pattern adds a recognition prefix, so more accounts can appear in the unmanaged-admin report (reported only, never disabled). It cannot be cleared (the save is refused). Reversible: restore the old pattern.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). Uses AdminTypePrefixes, EnvironmentSuffixes, AdminWord and TenantCommonName.
info.recommended: Decide it before the first admin is created and keep it stable; use {AdminWord} and {TenantCommonName} instead of literal text so the pattern can be copied to other tenants.

settings.label: AdminAccountPatternHighPriv (high-privilege admin name)
settings.where: Settings > Naming conventions (also Get Started > Naming)

info.what: The user name of a high-privilege (L0 / Tier 0) admin account, used when an admin row has Purpose = HighPriv. Note: the shipped pattern has no {AdminTypePrefix}, so external high-privilege admins get no x- unless you add it.
info.enabled: When set: new high-privilege admin names use it. It also adds an admin-recognition prefix, and on hybrid tenants an AD admin row with no Purpose whose name matches it is created in the high-privilege AD OU.
info.disabled: It cannot be saved blank: this is one of the four required naming keys, and the save is refused. A blank value left in the store by an older version makes the engine use the shipped default for it, with a warning in every run.
info.risk: Existing accounts keep their names. Changing it can move where new AD high-privilege accounts are created (a row with no Purpose may no longer match and go to the day-to-day OU). It cannot be cleared (the save is refused). Reversible: restore the old pattern.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). Works with AdminWord, EnvironmentSuffixes and the AD OU placement (High Priv Admins).
info.recommended: Keep a clear L0 / T0 marker in the name so high-privilege accounts are obvious in sign-in logs and route to the right AD OU.

info.what: Text added after the person's name in a new admin account's display name. Tokens such as {Initial} or {Platform} may be used.
info.enabled: When set to your own value: the Create admin wizard builds display names as the person's name plus your suffix, e.g. Jane Doe (ABC). The hybrid worker uses it for AD rows that carry no display name.
info.disabled: At the default ( (Admin)): the wizard does not use the suffix as written -- it builds a richer display name such as Jane Doe (Admin, <usage>, ID), and AD rows without a display name get Jane Doe (Admin).
info.risk: Only new accounts are affected; existing display names are not changed. Reversible: restore the old value.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). Nothing else.
info.recommended: Keep the default unless your organisation needs a specific display-name style for admin accounts.

info.what: The name starts that identify an admin account. The engine reads admin accounts from your tenant only where the user name starts with one of these, so ordinary users are never in scope. Tokens are allowed; only the part before the first unknown token is used.
info.enabled: When set: on the next engine run every account starting with a listed prefix is treated as an admin account. The engine always ALSO adds the starts of the two admin patterns and the shipped prefixes (Admin-, x-Admin, g-Admin), so you can widen recognition but not narrow it below those. Admin accounts with no row are reported as unmanaged, never disabled. On a managed tenant these prefixes are compared with incoming admins and a mismatch is reported.
info.disabled: When blank: the starts of the two admin patterns plus the shipped prefixes are used. If no prefix can be found at all, the engine refuses to read admins rather than scan every user.
info.risk: A too-broad prefix (e.g. a-) pulls ordinary users into the admin set; the engine then stops the run instead of acting on them. Accounts your rows name are always managed, whatever their name. Reversible: restore the old list; the next run uses it.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). The engine identity needs User.Read.All to read the matching accounts.
info.recommended: Leave it at the default unless you have existing admin accounts with another naming; then add their exact prefix, as specific as possible.

info.what: The admin type used when an admin row does not name one. It picks the prefix from the Prefix by admin type table. The list offers only the types that table defines.
info.enabled: When set: new admin names for rows without an admin type use that type's prefix, and the naming check before commit expects that prefix.
info.disabled: At the default: internal-adminuser (no prefix).
info.risk: Existing accounts are not renamed. Rows without an admin type may start showing naming warnings if their names were built with another prefix. Reversible: pick the old type again.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). Must be a type defined in Prefix by admin type.
info.recommended: Keep internal-adminuser and set the admin type explicitly on consultant and guest rows.

info.what: The environment used when a row does not name one. It picks the suffix from the Suffix by environment table, for admin names and for the {Platform} token in group names.
info.enabled: When set: new admin names and group names built from now on use that environment's suffix when nothing else says which environment applies.
info.disabled: At the default: entra (-ID).
info.risk: Existing names do not change, but new groups whose pattern contains {Platform} get a different suffix than older ones, and rows without an environment may draw naming warnings. Reversible: pick the old value.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). Must be an environment defined in Suffix by environment.
info.recommended: Keep entra; mark on-premises rows explicitly with Environment = ad.

settings.label: PimGroupPattern (PIM group name)
settings.where: Settings > Naming conventions (also Get Started > Naming)

info.what: The name of a PIM group, built around its tag ({Role}). It is also how PIM Manager and the engine recognise your groups: the literal text before the first token (PIM- by default) is the prefix used to find managed groups.
info.enabled: When set: new group names from the wizards and template packs use it. From the next engine run the literal prefix decides which groups the engine reads from the tenant, which groups may be retired, which groups the hybrid worker mirrors to AD (prefix + -S_AD), and how tags are read back from names.
info.disabled: It cannot be saved blank: this is one of the four required naming keys, and the save is refused. A blank value left in the store by an older version makes the engine use the shipped default for it, with a warning in every run.
info.risk: Existing groups are not renamed. Change the prefix and groups with the old prefix are only found where a definition names them exactly; retiring them is refused, and the AD mirror follows the new prefix instead. A pattern with no literal prefix makes prefix-based actions select nothing. Reversible: restore the old pattern; the next run recognises the old groups again.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). A separate group prefix setting, if set, overrides the prefix for retirement.
info.recommended: Decide it before the first group is created and keep a literal prefix of at least three characters (e.g. PIM- or GRP-) so the engine can prove which groups it owns.

info.what: The name of a permission group that grants an Entra role inside one administrative unit. {Role} is the tag without its AU part, {AdminUnit} the administrative unit.
info.enabled: When changed from the shipped value: the permission wizard names new AU-scoped groups with your pattern, with every token filled.
info.disabled: At the shipped value: AU-scoped groups keep the normal permission-group naming (the PIM group pattern around the tag, which already contains -AU-<unit>) -- the shipped value itself is not used to build names.
info.risk: Only new groups are affected; existing groups keep their names. Reversible: restore the shipped value.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). Nothing else.
info.recommended: Leave it at the shipped value unless your convention needs AU-scoped groups to look different from other permission groups.

info.what: Optional, advanced: a regular expression every group tag must match. It only drives the naming check before commit; it does not change any name and the engine does not use it to act.
info.enabled: When set: the check before commit warns about every group tag that does not match your expression. It replaces the built-in check completely, so a loose expression also stops the built-in warnings.
info.disabled: When blank: the built-in check -- the PIM group pattern shape, or the tiered -L#-T#- shape.
info.risk: Warnings only; nothing is blocked or changed in your tenant. An invalid expression is silently ignored and every tag then passes. Reversible: clear it.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). Nothing else.
info.recommended: Leave it blank unless you need stricter enforcement than the built-in check; test the expression on a few existing tags first.

info.what: Despite the key name, this is the name of a PERMISSION group (Entra role, Azure role, workload role) -- not an Azure resource group. Tokens: {Workload} / {Service}, {Scope}, {Permission}, {Level}, {Tier}, {Plane}, {Domain}, {Platform}.
info.enabled: When changed from the shipped value: the permission wizard names new permission groups with your pattern, every token filled; a token with no value disappears cleanly.
info.disabled: At the shipped value: permission groups keep the PIM group pattern around their tag. It cannot be saved blank (one of the four required naming keys); a blank value left by an older version makes the engine use the shipped default, with a warning.
info.risk: Only new groups are affected; existing permission groups keep their names. It cannot be cleared (the save is refused). Reversible: restore the shipped value.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). Nothing else.
info.recommended: Leave it at the shipped value unless your convention needs permission groups named differently from role groups.

info.what: The display name of an administrative unit that the Create access wizard adds for a new group type. {AdminUnit} is the administrative unit tag without its PIM- prefix (e.g. PIM-PROJECTS becomes PIM-Groups-PROJECTS).
info.enabled: When set: when the wizard stages a group whose administrative unit is not defined yet, the new administrative unit definition gets a name from your pattern; the engine creates it on the next run after you commit.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: PIM-Groups-{AdminUnit}.
