info.risk: Only administrative units staged from now on; existing ones keep their names. Reversible: restore the old value.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). The engine identity needs rights to create administrative units when one is staged.
info.recommended: Keep the default, or match the naming your directory already uses for administrative units.

settings.label: AD OU (Day2Day Admins)
settings.default: Blank (no AD admin accounts are created)

info.what: The on-premises Active Directory OU (distinguished name, e.g. OU=Admins,DC=example,DC=com) where new day-to-day admin accounts are created. Only for tenants with on-premises AD.
info.enabled: When set: on its next scheduled run the hybrid worker creates every due on-premises admin row (Environment / platform AD) that is not high-privilege as an AD user in this OU, with an initial password delivered to the admin mail recipient.
info.disabled: When blank: AD admin accounts are not created -- each one is skipped with the reason target OU empty. Cloud-only tenants leave it blank; nothing else depends on it.
info.risk: Setting it lets PIM Manager create accounts in your AD for the first time. Changing it only affects new accounts; existing accounts are never moved. Reversible: clear it and creation stops on the next run; accounts already created stay in AD.
info.requires: Pro (hybrid Active Directory) and a hybrid worker whose identity may create users in this OU. SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. The high-privilege OU is set separately.
info.recommended: Use a dedicated admin OU that is protected and excluded from sync to Entra ID; leave it blank if you have no on-premises AD.

settings.label: AD OU (High Priv Admins)
settings.default: Blank (no high-privilege AD admin accounts are created)

info.what: The on-premises AD OU where new high-privilege (L0 / Tier 0) admin accounts are created -- rows with Purpose = HighPriv, or with no Purpose and a user name that matches the high-privilege admin pattern.
info.enabled: When set: on its next scheduled run the hybrid worker creates due high-privilege AD admin rows as AD users in this OU.
info.disabled: When blank: high-privilege AD admin accounts are skipped with the reason target OU empty; they are NOT placed in the day-to-day OU instead.
info.risk: Setting it lets PIM Manager create Tier 0 accounts in your AD. Existing accounts are never moved when you change it. Reversible: clear it and creation stops; accounts already created stay.
info.requires: Pro (hybrid Active Directory) and a hybrid worker allowed to create users in this OU. SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Uses AdminAccountPatternHighPriv to classify rows without a Purpose.
info.recommended: Point it at your Tier 0 admin OU, protected like other Tier 0 objects, so high-privilege accounts never land with ordinary admins.

settings.label: Filters
settings.default: Four filters: Admins, PIM-managed groups (all), PIM resource groups (AD-sync), PIM service groups (AD-sync)

info.what: Name-marker filters, each with a key, a label, any-of patterns (with *) and markers every match must also contain. They are kept for compatibility with the earlier engine generation.
info.enabled: When set: the filters are stored and shown here, and copied with the settings-copy tool. The current engine and PIM Manager do not use them to select admins or groups -- admin accounts are found through the admin account prefixes and groups through the PIM group pattern.
info.disabled: The list cannot be empty: if it is, PIM Manager seeds the four default filters again, and saving an empty list is refused.
info.risk: Editing them has no effect on what the engine reads or changes. Reversible.
info.requires: SuperAdmin in PIM Manager. Free (Community). Nothing else.
info.recommended: Leave the defaults. To change which accounts or groups PIM Manager recognises, use AdminAccountPatterns and PimGroupPattern instead.

settings.label: AD group marker
settings.where: Settings > Hybrid AD & workloads > Hybrid Active Directory (PIM for AD)

info.what: The text at the end of a PIM group name that marks the group as also existing in your on-premises Active Directory. The hybrid worker mirrors every defined PIM group named <your group prefix>*<marker> to an AD security group of the same name, and keeps that AD group's members in step with who has the PIM group activated. The marker is also the {marker} part of the per-server group name.
info.enabled: When set: only defined PIM groups ending in this marker are mirrored and synced. Groups that newly match are created in AD (if an OU for new AD groups is set) and their members synced: users carrying the AD admin suffix without an active PIM activation are removed. The hybrid worker's change check picks up a saved value on its next pass and re-runs the group mirror at once.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: the marker -S_AD is used, so groups named like <prefix>*-S_AD are mirrored (the shape the older PIM-for-AD scripts used).
info.risk: Changing the marker changes which AD groups the worker manages. Groups that stop matching are no longer synced: their current AD members are left as they are and no longer removed when an activation ends. Groups that start matching get non-activated PIM-managed users removed. Nothing is deleted from AD. Reversible: set the old marker back; the next pass syncs the old groups again.
info.requires: Pro (On-premises Active Directory feature) and a running hybrid worker. SuperAdmin to change. The worker needs Graph Group.Read.All, User.Read.All and PrivilegedAssignmentSchedule.Read.AzureADGroup, and AD rights on the groups. Ignored when Pattern override is set.
info.recommended: Keep -S_AD unless your groups already use another marker. Change it only together with renaming your PIM groups.

settings.label: Pattern override
settings.where: Settings > Hybrid AD & workloads > Hybrid Active Directory (PIM for AD)
settings.default: Blank (derived: your group prefix + * + the AD group marker)

info.what: A full wildcard that replaces the derived pattern for which PIM groups are mirrored to AD. Only groups defined in PIM Manager are ever considered -- the pattern never reaches AD groups PIM Manager does not define. The card's preview shows the effective pattern and how many defined groups match today.
info.enabled: When set: every defined PIM group whose name matches the wildcard is mirrored to AD and has its AD membership synced from active PIM activations. The value must contain * and may not be * alone. The marker setting is then ignored for matching.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: the pattern is derived from your naming -- your group name prefix + * + the AD group marker (for example PIM-*-S_AD).
info.risk: A wider pattern brings more groups under the sync: in each newly matched AD group, users carrying the AD admin suffix who have no active PIM activation are removed, and an existing AD group of the same name is adopted. A narrower pattern leaves dropped groups unmanaged with their members in place. Reversible: clear the field; the derived pattern applies on the next pass.
info.requires: Pro (On-premises Active Directory feature) and a running hybrid worker. SuperAdmin to change. Overrides HybridAdGroupMarker for matching.
info.recommended: Leave blank. Set it only when your AD-backed groups do not follow the prefix-plus-marker shape, and check the preview count before saving.

settings.label: Cloud admin suffix
settings.where: Settings > Hybrid AD & workloads > Hybrid Active Directory (PIM for AD)
settings.default: Blank (the Entra suffix of your naming conventions, -ID as shipped)

info.what: The end of a cloud admin account name (its mail nickname) that the hybrid worker swaps for the AD admin suffix to find the matching on-premises account. Example: Admin-JDOE-ID in Entra ID becomes Admin-JDOE-AD in AD. Only a trailing suffix is swapped; a name without it maps to the same name in AD.
info.enabled: When set: activated members are mapped to AD accounts with this suffix swapped out. A changed value changes which AD account is added to a group when someone activates the PIM group, from the next sync pass.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: the Entra suffix from your naming conventions is used (-ID as shipped). If your conventions name no suffix, accounts map to the same name in AD.
info.risk: A wrong suffix maps people to AD accounts that do not exist (the add fails and the sync reports failures) or to the wrong account. Accounts added under the old mapping no longer count as wanted and are removed if they carry the AD admin suffix. Reversible: set the right value; the next pass corrects the membership.
info.requires: Pro (On-premises Active Directory feature) and a running hybrid worker. SuperAdmin to change. Works together with HybridAdAccountSuffix.
info.recommended: Leave blank so it follows your naming conventions; set it only when your cloud admin names use a different ending than the conventions say.

settings.label: AD admin suffix
settings.where: Settings > Hybrid AD & workloads > Hybrid Active Directory (PIM for AD)
settings.default: Blank (the AD suffix of your naming conventions, -AD as shipped)

info.what: The end of the AD admin account a cloud admin maps to, and the safety marker for removals: the sync only ever removes a USER from a mirrored AD group when its account name ends in this suffix. Service accounts, nested groups and users without the suffix are always kept and reported as not PIM-managed.
info.enabled: When set: activated members are added as <name><suffix> in AD, and every user in a mirrored group that carries this suffix but has no active PIM activation is removed on the next sync pass (the sync runs continuously on the hybrid worker).
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: the AD suffix from your naming conventions is used (-AD as shipped). If neither names a suffix, the sync adds members but removes nobody.
info.risk: Setting a suffix that other accounts in those AD groups also carry makes those accounts removable: they are taken out of the mirrored groups unless they have an active PIM activation or are listed under Never remove. Reversible for future passes, but removed memberships are only re-added when the person activates again.
info.requires: Pro (On-premises Active Directory feature) and a running hybrid worker. SuperAdmin to change. Works together with HybridAdCloudSuffix and HybridAdProtectedMembers.
info.recommended: Leave blank to follow your naming conventions. Use a suffix only your PIM-created AD admin accounts carry.

settings.label: OU for new AD groups
settings.where: Settings > Hybrid AD & workloads > Hybrid Active Directory (PIM for AD)
settings.default: Blank (groups are never created, only kept in sync)

info.what: The distinguished name of the organizational unit (OU=...,DC=...) where the hybrid worker creates AD groups for mirrored PIM groups that do not exist in AD yet. Groups are created as global security groups with the PIM group's name, a display name of <name> (separate group) and its description.
info.enabled: When set: on the next group mirror run (hourly, and at once when the worker sees the change) every mirrored PIM group missing in AD is created in this OU; the continuous sync then fills it with the people who have it activated. Existing groups elsewhere keep their place and have their display name and description corrected.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: missing AD groups are never created -- they are reported as skipped, and only groups that already exist in AD are kept in sync.
info.risk: The worker starts creating objects in your AD. Groups it created are not deleted again when you clear the setting or remove the PIM group. A wrong OU makes the creates fail (access denied or no such object), reported on the job. Reversible: clear the field to stop creating; remove unwanted groups by hand.
info.requires: Pro (On-premises Active Directory feature) and a running hybrid worker whose managed service account may create groups in this OU (the AD setup script grants this with -GroupsOu). SuperAdmin to change.
info.recommended: Set it to a dedicated OU for PIM groups once the worker is in place, so a new AD-marked PIM group reaches AD without manual work.

settings.label: Per-server group format
settings.where: Settings > Hybrid AD & workloads > Hybrid Active Directory (PIM for AD)

info.what: The name of the per-server permission group that becomes local administrator on one server. Tokens: {prefix} (your group prefix), {server} (required), {cloud} (the cloud admin suffix) and {marker} (the AD group marker). Server onboarding lists your Windows servers, Discovery offers this group for each one, and once it is defined and mirrored the worker adds it to that server's local Administrators. The server-group sync lane also uses this name to tell server groups from critical groups.
info.enabled: When set: Discovery offers groups with the new name, and server onboarding (hourly) looks for the group with the new name on each server. Groups defined under the old format are no longer treated as server groups.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: {prefix}AD-SRV-{server}{cloud}{marker} is used, the naming the older PIM-for-AD scripts used.
info.risk: Groups under the old name stay in the servers' local Administrators -- onboarding only adds, never removes. If the new name does not match the mirror pattern (for example without {marker}), the new groups are never mirrored to AD and never reach the servers. Reversible: set the old format back.
info.requires: Pro (On-premises Active Directory feature), a running hybrid worker and its server identity as local administrator on the servers. SuperAdmin to change. Depends on HybridAdGroupMarker and HybridAdCloudSuffix.
info.recommended: Keep the default unless your existing server groups use another shape; keep {marker} in it so the groups are mirrored.

settings.label: Shared server-admins group
settings.where: Settings > Hybrid AD & workloads > Hybrid Active Directory (PIM for AD)

info.what: One AD group (name, or DOMAIN\name) that server onboarding also adds to the local Administrators group of every onboarded server -- next to that server's own per-server group. It replaces the shared all-servers group of the older PIM-for-AD scripts.
info.enabled: When set: on the next server onboarding run (hourly) the worker adds this group to local Administrators on every server whose per-server group is defined and already exists in AD. Its members become local administrators on all those servers.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: only each server's own per-server group is added.
info.risk: This widens who is local administrator on every onboarded server. Onboarding only adds: clearing the setting or changing the group does NOT remove it from the servers -- you remove it by hand. Do not use a PIM just-in-time (mirrored) group here, and do not rely on it for the worker's own rights: the worker gets its server rights through its own permission group.
info.requires: Pro (On-premises Active Directory feature), a running hybrid worker whose server identity is local administrator on the servers (set by the servers GPO from the AD setup script). SuperAdmin to change.
info.recommended: Leave blank unless you deliberately want one group with admin rights on all servers; prefer the per-server groups with just-in-time activation.

settings.label: Never remove
settings.where: Settings > Hybrid AD & workloads > Hybrid Active Directory (PIM for AD)

info.what: Account names (comma or semicolon separated, no wildcards) that the just-in-time sync never removes from a mirrored AD group, even when they carry the AD admin suffix and have no active PIM activation. They are reported as kept (protected).
info.enabled: When set: the listed accounts keep their membership in every mirrored AD group permanently, from the next sync pass. People with an active activation are still added as usual.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: every user carrying the AD admin suffix without an active PIM activation is removed from the mirrored groups. Users without that suffix, service accounts and nested groups are kept anyway.
info.risk: A listed account keeps standing privileged membership in AD, outside just-in-time control. Clearing the list makes those accounts removable at once: the next pass takes them out of every mirrored group where they have no active activation. Reversible: edit the list; removed memberships come back only through a new activation or by hand.
info.requires: Pro (On-premises Active Directory feature) and a running hybrid worker. SuperAdmin to change. Only matters for accounts that carry the AD admin suffix.
info.recommended: Keep it empty or to a short list of break-glass or emergency AD accounts you have documented.

settings.label: Groups per batch
settings.where: Settings > Hybrid AD & workloads > Hybrid Active Directory (PIM for AD)

info.what: How many mirrored groups one parallel batch reads from Microsoft Graph per sync pass when the worker looks up who has each group activated. Allowed 1-1000. It is a speed setting only -- it does not change who is added or removed.
info.enabled: When set: the groups of a sync pass are cut into batches of this size, each read in its own parallel runspace (PowerShell 7) through Graph batch calls. It applies to both sync lanes, server groups and critical groups.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: 50 groups per batch.
info.risk: Very large batches make each runspace slower and can hit Graph throttling; very small ones add overhead. A throttled or failed read is retried one by one, so membership is not lost -- only the time an activation takes to reach AD grows. Reversible: change the number.
info.requires: Pro (On-premises Active Directory feature), a running hybrid worker on PowerShell 7 (on Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads are one by one). SuperAdmin to change. Works with HybridAdSyncParallel.
info.recommended: Keep 50. Tune only with many hundreds of server groups, together with Batches at once.

settings.label: Batches at once
settings.where: Settings > Hybrid AD & workloads > Hybrid Active Directory (PIM for AD)

info.what: How many group batches the hybrid worker reads from Microsoft Graph at the same time during a sync pass. Allowed 1-64. Higher is faster until Graph starts throttling. It does not change who is added or removed.
info.enabled: When set: up to this many batches run in parallel on PowerShell 7. A value of 1 reads the groups one by one.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: 8 batches at once.
info.risk: Too high causes Graph throttling and more CPU and memory on the worker; throttled reads are retried one by one, so the effect is slower syncs, not wrong membership. Reversible: change the number.
info.requires: Pro (On-premises Active Directory feature), a running hybrid worker on PowerShell 7. SuperAdmin to change. Works with HybridAdSyncBatchSize.
info.recommended: Keep 8. Raise it only if activations of server groups reach AD too slowly and the worker logs show no throttling.

settings.label: Company name
settings.where: Settings > Access requests (RFA) > Request portal: company name & support

info.what: The company name shown on the public access request portal, so people can see where they are signing in. It appears in the page header and the browser tab title. Plain text, at most 40 characters.
info.enabled: When set: the engine's request-portal sync (every minute) publishes the name to the portal, and the portal shows it from the next page load.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: no company name is shown on the portal.
info.risk: The portal is public, so anyone who opens it sees the name. Nothing else changes. Reversible: clear or edit it; the portal follows within about a minute.
info.requires: Pro (Request for authorization portal) with the portal deployed -- without it the value is stored but never shown. SuperAdmin to change; Admin can read it.
info.recommended: Set your organization's name so people recognise the portal before they enter their address.

settings.label: Support e-mail
settings.where: Settings > Access requests (RFA) > Request portal: company name & support

info.what: One e-mail address shown on the public access request portal as a 'Need help? Contact ...' line with a mail link. A value that is not an e-mail address is refused at save and never published.
info.enabled: When set: the engine's request-portal sync (every minute) publishes the address and the portal shows the help line on its pages from the next load.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: no help line is shown; people on the portal have no contact pointer.
info.risk: The address is visible to anyone who opens the public portal, so expect unsolicited mail on it. Use a shared support mailbox, not a person. Reversible: clear or edit it.
info.requires: Pro (Request for authorization portal) with the portal deployed -- without it the value is stored but never shown. SuperAdmin to change; Admin can read it.
info.recommended: Set your IT service desk's shared mailbox, such as it-support@example.com.

settings.label: RFA store account
settings.where: Settings > Access requests (RFA) > RFA broker & API
settings.default: Blank until the request portal is deployed (the deploy script fills it in)

info.what: The Azure storage account shared by the public request portal and the engine. The portal writes requests there; the engine pulls them every minute with its managed identity, re-decides each one, and writes back status, the eligibility list and the API settings. The public side never reaches PIM directly.
info.enabled: When set: the request-portal sync runs every minute against this account -- taking in portal and API requests, enabling accounts and ad-hoc memberships, ending them when time is up, and sending the mails.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: the request-portal sync takes in no requests and the portal is shown as not deployed -- but an access window that is still open is closed when it ends (the account is disabled again). IT overrides in the Manager still work.
info.risk: Blank or a wrong account stops new requests and the portal updates (the sync job reports it as failed), but the step that DISABLES accounts and removes ad-hoc memberships when their window ends keeps running -- access never stays on past its window. Pointing it at another store makes the engine act on that store's requests. Reversible: set the right account back; the next run catches up.
info.requires: Pro (Request for authorization portal). The engine's managed identity needs Storage Table Data Contributor on the account (granted by the portal deploy). SuperAdmin to change. 3-24 lower-case letters and digits.
info.recommended: Leave the value the portal deploy wrote; change it only when you redeploy the portal to a new storage account.

settings.label: Public portal URL
settings.where: Settings > Access requests (RFA) > RFA broker & API
settings.default: Blank until the request portal is deployed (the deploy script fills it in)

info.what: The https address of the public request portal. PIM Manager uses it as the link in mails to people who request access (enabled, ending, ended, denied), in the consultant company review mails, as the portal link on the Access requests page, and to show where the API description lives (<url>/api/v1/openapi.json). It does not move the portal itself.
info.enabled: When set: mails sent from the next sync run carry this link, and the Access requests page shows it to copy and hand out. It must start with https://.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: mails go out without a portal link, the Access requests page shows no portal link, and company review mails cannot point contacts to the portal.
info.risk: A wrong URL sends people to a page that does not answer, or to the wrong site. Nothing in access changes. Reversible: correct it; the next mails use the new link.
info.requires: Pro (Request for authorization portal). SuperAdmin to change.
info.recommended: Leave the value the portal deploy wrote, or set your own custom domain for the portal if you add one.

settings.label: API applications (client ids)
settings.where: Settings > Access requests (RFA) > RFA broker & API
settings.default: Empty (no application may call the API)

info.what: The Entra application (client) ids allowed to call the access request REST API, typically your ticketing system. The engine publishes the list to the portal for a fast answer and re-checks every API request itself.
info.enabled: When set: a listed application can request, through the API, that an admin account is enabled for 1-744 hours or that an account gets a timed group membership. API requests are approved on arrival -- no department owner decision -- and the engine applies them on its next run, within a few minutes. It can also send proposals, which only become pending changes for an administrator.
info.disabled: When empty / at the default: every API call made with an Entra application token is refused. API keys still work if you create them.
info.risk: Each listed application can grant timed privileged access without a second person in PIM Manager, so the approval must happen in that system. API group requests are not limited to the ad-hoc group list. Reversible: remove the id; the engine refuses its new requests on the next run, but access already granted runs until its end time.
info.requires: Pro (Request for authorization portal and the access request API). SuperAdmin to change. Values must be application (client) ids (GUIDs).
info.recommended: List only the one application of your ticketing system, and make sure its own workflow requires approval before it calls the API.

settings.label: Ad-hoc groups consultants may request
settings.where: Settings > Access requests (RFA) > RFA broker & API

info.what: The permission groups that people using the request portal (typically consultants) may ask to join for a short time, in addition to the access they already have. Only defined groups are offered, and a group the account already holds is not shown.
info.enabled: When set: the next sync run (every minute) publishes the offered groups to each eligible account on the portal. A request always waits for an Owner of the person's department, who is mailed and must decide within 24 hours. On approval the engine adds an active, time-limited membership on its next run and removes it automatically when the time is up.
info.disabled: When none are selected / at the default: the portal offers no groups to request; only enabling the person's own admin account can be requested.
info.risk: Every listed group becomes requestable by every portal-eligible account, so a department owner's approval is the only gate. Choose groups whose rights you are willing to hand out for hours. Reversible: deselect a group; it is no longer offered, but memberships already granted run until their end time.
info.requires: Pro (Request for authorization portal) with the portal deployed. Department owners must be set, or nobody can approve. SuperAdmin to change. Length offered: Default ad-hoc length plus the department's own durations.
info.recommended: Start with none, then add a few low-to-medium impact groups that consultants regularly need for short tasks.

settings.label: Default ad-hoc length (hours)
settings.where: Settings > Access requests (RFA) > RFA broker & API

info.what: The length offered on the portal for an ad-hoc group membership, from 1 to 744 hours (31 days). The portal offers this value together with the request durations set on the person's department. When the time is up the membership is removed automatically.
info.enabled: When set: from the next sync run the portal offers this length for every ad-hoc group request; requests already approved keep the length they were granted with.
info.disabled: When blank / at the default: 24 hours is offered, plus the department's own durations.
info.risk: A long default keeps privileged group membership in place for days without a new decision. Reversible: lower it; new requests use the new length, existing memberships end at their original time.
info.requires: Pro (Request for authorization portal). Only matters when ad-hoc groups are offered. SuperAdmin to change.
info.recommended: Keep 24 hours or less; long-term access belongs in the delegation grid, not in ad-hoc requests.

settings.label: API keys
settings.where: Settings > Access requests (RFA) > RFA broker & API

info.what: Keys for systems that cannot use an Entra application token to call the access request API. Each key has a name, scopes (requests.write to submit, requests.read to read status) and a lifetime of 1-3650 days. The key is shown once; only its hash is stored. It is sent as the X-Api-Key header.
info.enabled: When a key is created: the next request-portal sync (within a minute or two) publishes its hash to the portal, and a caller with requests.write can then ask for admin accounts to be enabled or timed group memberships to be added -- approved on arrival and applied by the engine on its next run.
info.disabled: When no key exists (the default) or a key is revoked: calls with it are refused. The engine refuses a revoked key at once; the portal stops accepting it within a few minutes.
info.risk: Anyone holding a write key can grant timed privileged access without an approver in PIM Manager. A key cannot be shown again; if it leaks, revoke it. Expired keys stop working by themselves. Revoking does not end access already granted -- it runs until its end time.
info.requires: Pro (access request API). SuperAdmin to create, list and revoke keys. The request portal must be deployed.
info.recommended: Prefer an allow-listed Entra application. If you need a key, give it only the scope it needs and the shortest lifetime that works, and store it in a secret vault.

settings.label: Allow an administrator to approve their own requests

info.what: Separation of duties for approval requests (offboard, revoke and similar): by default the administrator who raises a request may not approve it -- a different administrator must. This switch lifts that rule for tenants with only one PIM Manager administrator.
info.enabled: When on: takes effect at once. The person who raised a request can approve it on the Approvals page, and an offboarding change (offboard, Removed, Deleted) committed in the admin grid is committed straight away instead of being held for a second person. Each such decision is recorded as self-approved in the audit, and the card shows who switched it on and when.
info.disabled: When off (the default): a request waits until another Admin or SuperAdmin decides it; disabling changes committed in the grid are held as approval requests.
info.risk: One administrator alone can offboard accounts and revoke access, with no second pair of eyes -- a mistake or a compromised administrator account is not caught. Reversible: switch it off; requests raised from then on wait for a second person again. Decisions already made stand.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: Off. Switch it on only while your tenant has a single PIM Manager administrator, and off again as soon as a second one exists.

settings.label: Give new department owners Reader access (their normal account)
settings.where: Access > Departments & owners (also Get Started > Departments & owners)

info.what: Department owners approve access requests and receive the mail about their department, and the links in that mail open PIM Manager. This sets whether the tick 'Give PIM Manager Reader access (their normal account)' is on when you add an owner. It applies to departments saved on the page, in Get Started and through the Entra and CSV imports.
info.enabled: When on (the default): an owner who is new in a save and is not yet a PIM Manager user is added to Manager access as a Reader with their normal account, and the page says who was added. Someone who already has a role keeps it unchanged -- never upgraded, never downgraded. You can still untick it for a single owner before you save.
info.disabled: When off: the tick starts off, and imports add nobody. Owners still approve and receive mail; the links open only for those you give access under Manager access & roles yourself.
info.risk: Low. Reader is view-only: a Reader sees configuration and assignments but cannot change anything. Removing an owner does not remove their role -- the page lists them so you decide. Reversible: switch it off; Readers already added stay until you remove them.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it and to save departments. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: On. Approving others never needs an admin account; create one only for an owner who will hold a privileged role themselves.

settings.label: Deployment rings
settings.where: Settings > Deployment rings (managing tenant only); also on MSP > Managed tenant registry
settings.default: Three rings: 0 Dev, 1 Test, 2 Broad, no tag rules

info.what: The rings that stage what a managing tenant replicates (central admins, delegations and other ring-tagged rows). A row on ring N reaches the managed tenants whose own ring is N or lower, so ring 0 gets new rows first and the highest ring is the broadest. Each ring has a name and an optional tag rule (tag:region:eu, tag:a+b for all-of, tenant:<id>) that narrows which tenants on it count. Each managed tenant still sets its own ring locally.
info.enabled: When saved: the rings are read back, every ring picker follows at once, and a publish is requested -- the rings reach the managed tenants in the next signed bundle (within about 5 minutes). A tenant on a ring whose tag rule it does not match receives nothing ring-gated until it matches. Up to 10 rings (0-9), numbered without gaps.
info.disabled: At the default: rings 0 Dev, 1 Test and 2 Broad with no tag rules -- every managed tenant on a ring is a member of it.
info.risk: A tag rule that a tenant does not match withholds new and changed rows from that tenant: it keeps what it already has (nothing is retracted) but gets no updates. Removing the highest ring is refused while a tenant or a row still uses it. Reversible: edit or clear the rule and save; the next bundle delivers the held rows.
info.requires: Pro (multi-tenant), on the managing tenant only. SuperAdmin to change. Tags come from the managed tenant registry.
info.recommended: Keep the three default rings, put one or two test tenants on ring 0 or 1, and use tag rules only when you need to narrow a ring to a region or customer group.

settings.label: How PIM Manager sends mail
settings.where: Settings > Mail & alerting > Mail sending (also Get Started > Mail sender)

info.what: Picks the one transport every PIM Manager mail uses -- TAP codes, approval and review mails, alerts, the daily digest and the tier report. Shared mailbox sends through Microsoft Graph as the environment's own identity from one Exchange Online mailbox. SMTP relay sends through a mail server you already run. None switches mail off.
info.enabled: When set: Shared mailbox needs the sender mailbox filled in; SMTP relay needs server, port and From address. The PIM Manager uses the new choice at once; scheduled jobs and the engine pick it up on their next run. Choosing None makes every send return 'not sent' -- new admin accounts then cannot receive their TAP by mail, and the engine reports that instead of pretending it was delivered.
info.disabled: At the default (Shared mailbox) and with no sender mailbox set, mail is rendered but not sent, and the Alerting card and Get Started show 'configure to enable'.
info.risk: None (or a broken relay) silently stops all PIM mail, including alerts about failures and TAP codes for new admins. The None option only appears in the form when mail is already off, so in practice you switch between Shared mailbox and SMTP relay. Reversible: pick another mode and save; mails that were not sent meanwhile are not re-sent.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. Shared mailbox: an Exchange Online plan and a one-time setup by an Exchange or Global Administrator that grants Mail.Send scoped to that one mailbox (never tenant-wide). SMTP relay: a reachable relay and, if it needs sign-in, the password in Key Vault. The Email alerting feature (Settings > Feature customization) must be on, or nothing is sent in any mode.
info.recommended: Shared mailbox -- no password to manage, and the send right is limited to one mailbox. Use SMTP relay only when your organisation requires all mail to leave through its own relay.

settings.label: Shared mailbox: name, domain and display name
settings.where: Settings > Mail & alerting > Mail sending (also Get Started > Mail sender)
settings.default: PIM-Engine at the tenant's initial domain, display name 'PIM Manager (notifications)'

info.what: The Exchange Online shared mailbox PIM Manager sends as when the mail mode is Shared mailbox -- named by your organisation: the mailbox name, one of the tenant's verified domains and the display name (step 1 of Get Started > Mail sender). The setup command is built from these values (-MailboxName, -MailDomain, -DisplayName). Step 2, Check and send a test mail, makes that mailbox the sender. Every mail is sent from this address through Microsoft Graph.
info.enabled: When set: the PIM Manager sends from this mailbox immediately; the engine and scheduled jobs use it from their next run. A changed address makes the earlier test-mail proof stale, so Get Started shows the step as not done until a new test mail succeeds.
info.disabled: When blank: in Shared mailbox mode nothing is sent -- mails are rendered only, TAP delivery is refused as 'no sender configured', and alerts show 'configure to enable'.
info.risk: If the identity may not send as this mailbox (the setup script was not run for it), every send fails with a permission error -- the Mail check and the test mail show it. Clearing the field in the form does not clear the stored address; enter another address instead. Reversible at any time.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. Mail mode Shared mailbox. The setup script (run once by an Exchange or Global Administrator, browser sign-in) must have scoped Mail.Send for the PIM Manager and engine identities to exactly this mailbox. A shared mailbox needs no licence once the tenant has an Exchange Online plan.
info.recommended: Let the setup script create a dedicated shared mailbox with your own naming, so the send right covers only that one mailbox and nothing else in your tenant. The Exchange scope and role-assignment names follow the mailbox name (-ScopeName / -AssignmentNamePrefix to choose them yourself).

settings.label: Server / Port
settings.where: Settings > Mail & alerting > Mail sending > SMTP relay (also Get Started > Mail sender)

info.what: The host name and port of the SMTP relay PIM Manager hands its mail to when the mail mode is SMTP relay, for example smtp.example.com on port 587.
info.enabled: When set: every PIM mail -- including TAP codes for new admin accounts -- is handed to this server. The PIM Manager uses it at once; the engine and scheduled jobs from their next run. Port 465 (implicit TLS) is refused; use 587 with STARTTLS. A changed server makes the earlier test-mail proof stale.
info.disabled: When blank: SMTP relay mode cannot be saved, and an environment left in SMTP mode without a valid relay renders mail but sends nothing, reporting 'the SMTP relay is not configured correctly'.
info.risk: Your relay receives the content of every PIM mail, including one-time TAP codes, so it must be a server you trust and control. A wrong host or a firewall in between makes every send fail (shown in the Mail check and the test mail). Reversible: correct the server or switch back to Shared mailbox.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. Mail mode SMTP relay. Outbound network access from the PIM Manager and the engine to that host and port. A From address is also required.
info.recommended: Use your organisation's authenticated relay on port 587 with STARTTLS, and send a test mail after every change.

settings.label: Encryption
settings.where: Settings > Mail & alerting > Mail sending > SMTP relay (also Get Started > Mail sender)

info.what: Whether the connection to the SMTP relay is encrypted with STARTTLS or sent in clear text (None). Only STARTTLS on a plain port is supported; implicit TLS on port 465 is not.
info.enabled: When set to None: mail, the relay user name and password, and any TAP codes travel unencrypted between PIM Manager and the relay. Takes effect for the PIM Manager at once and for the engine and jobs on their next run.
info.disabled: At the default (STARTTLS): the connection is upgraded to TLS before the relay sign-in and the message are sent; a relay that does not offer STARTTLS makes the send fail.
info.risk: None exposes the relay password and the mail content, including one-time TAP codes, to anyone who can see the network path. Use it only for an internal relay on a network you control. Reversible: switch back to STARTTLS and save.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. Mail mode SMTP relay with a server configured.
info.recommended: STARTTLS. Choose None only for an internal relay that cannot do TLS and accepts no sign-in.

settings.label: From address
settings.where: Settings > Mail & alerting > Mail sending > SMTP relay (also Get Started > Mail sender)

info.what: The sender address on every mail PIM Manager sends through the SMTP relay, for example pim@example.com. Recipients see it as the sender; your relay may require that it is an address it is allowed to send for.
info.enabled: When set: every relay mail is sent from this address -- by the PIM Manager at once, by the engine and jobs from their next run. A changed address makes the earlier test-mail proof stale.
info.disabled: When blank: SMTP relay settings cannot be saved; the form and the server both refuse it.
info.risk: If the relay or your mail protection (SPF/DMARC) does not accept this address, mails are refused or land in spam -- TAP codes and alerts then do not arrive. Reversible: change the address and send a test mail.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. Mail mode SMTP relay. The relay must allow sending as this address.
info.recommended: A dedicated address in your own domain that the relay is permitted to send for, so recipients can recognise and trust PIM mail.

settings.label: User name / Password / Key Vault that keeps the password / Secret name
settings.where: Settings > Mail & alerting > Mail sending > SMTP relay (also Get Started > Mail sender)
settings.default: Blank user name (relay needs no sign-in); secret name PIM-SmtpRelayPassword

info.what: The sign-in PIM Manager uses on the SMTP relay. The user name, Key Vault name and secret name are stored with the settings; the password itself is written only to your environment's Key Vault and is never stored in the settings, never shown again and never written to a log.
info.enabled: When set: at every send the PIM Manager and the engine read the password from that Key Vault secret and sign in to the relay with the user name. Typing a new password replaces the secret; leaving the box empty keeps the existing one. If PIM Manager may not write the vault, the save tells you and shows a one-time command (browser sign-in) for someone who may.
info.disabled: When the user name is blank: PIM Manager connects to the relay without signing in (an anonymous internal relay). A password without a user name is refused.
info.risk: If the identities cannot read the secret, or the secret is empty, every relay send fails with that reason (the Mail check shows it). A wrong vault name or a rotated password at the relay has the same effect. Reversible: correct the values or store a new password.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. Mail mode SMTP relay. The PIM Manager and engine identities need Key Vault Secrets User on the secret to read it; the PIM Manager needs permission to write secrets in that vault to store a typed password (otherwise use the provided command).
info.recommended: Use an authenticated relay with a dedicated service account, keep the password in the environment's own Key Vault under the default secret name, and rotate it there.

settings.label: Email kill switch -- turn ALL outbound email off

info.what: An emergency stop for every email PIM Manager sends: alerts, the daily digest, the tier report, TAP codes, approval, review and reminder mails, and test mails. It is checked at the single point every mail passes through.
info.enabled: When on: every email is dropped with the reason 'email kill switch on'. The PIM Manager stops at once; the engine and scheduled jobs stop from their next run. New admin accounts cannot receive their TAP by mail, and the engine reports that. The Teams/generic alert webhook and Teams/Slack TAP chat delivery are not email and keep working.
info.disabled: When off: mail is sent normally through the configured mail sending, subject to the redirect and allowlist.
info.risk: Nobody is mailed about failures, drift, break-glass use or safety-breaker trips while it is on, and mails dropped meanwhile are never re-sent. Reversible: switch it off and save; the PIM Manager resumes at once, jobs and the engine from their next run.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role in PIM Manager. Nothing else.
info.recommended: Off. Use it only briefly -- for example while you fix a misbehaving template or a wrong recipient list -- and configure the alert webhook if you still need to be told about failures meanwhile.

info.what: A test and lab control: every PIM Manager email is sent to this one address instead of its real recipient. The original recipient is kept in the mail so you can see who it was meant for.
info.enabled: When set: alerts, digests, TAP codes, approval and review mails all go only to this address -- in the PIM Manager at once, in the engine and scheduled jobs from their next run. The allowlist is then checked against this address.
info.disabled: When blank: every mail goes to its real recipient.
info.risk: Whoever reads this mailbox receives every TAP code and therefore can sign in as any new admin account; real owners, approvers and admins receive nothing. Clearing it stops the redirect at once in the running PIM Manager, and in the engine and jobs from their next run. Reversible.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role in PIM Manager. A working mail sending setup.
info.recommended: Blank in production. Set it only in a test environment, to a mailbox that only the test team can read.

settings.label: Allowlist (one address per line; empty = no restriction)

info.what: Limits PIM Manager email to the listed addresses. Any recipient not on the list is dropped; a mail with several recipients keeps only the listed ones. Matching is on the full address, not case-sensitive, and wildcards or whole domains are not supported.
info.enabled: When set: only listed addresses receive mail -- alerts, digests, TAP codes, approval and review mails alike. The PIM Manager applies it at once; the engine and scheduled jobs from their next run. If a redirect is set, the redirect address must be on the list or nothing is sent.
info.disabled: When empty: there is no restriction; every resolved recipient is mailed.
info.risk: Anyone not listed -- new admins waiting for their TAP, approvers, department owners -- silently stops getting mail, and dropped mails are never re-sent. Reversible: add the address or empty the list.
info.requires: SuperAdmin role in PIM Manager. A working mail sending setup.
info.recommended: Empty in production. Use it in test or pilot environments to make sure mail can only reach the pilot group.

settings.label: Recipients (one email per line)
settings.where: Settings > Mail & alerting > Alerting (also Get Started > Alert recipients)

info.what: Who is mailed when PIM Manager raises an alert: job and engine failures, drift, expiring access, break-glass use, coverage gaps, missing targets and uncommitted changes. The same list receives the safety-breaker mails, the daily digest and the tier report unless those have their own lists, and it is the last fallback for TAP mails nobody else can receive.
info.enabled: When set: each recipient gets one mail per alert. Alerts raised in the PIM Manager use the list at once; the engine and scheduled jobs read it at each run. Addresses that do not look like mail addresses are dropped when you save.
info.disabled: When empty: alerts are prepared but nobody is mailed (only the alert webhook, if configured, still fires), safety-breaker trips report 'no alert recipient', and the digest and tier report go only to their own lists.
info.risk: Removing everyone means nobody hears about failed runs, held safety breakers or break-glass use. Alerts are recorded in Recent alerts either way. Reversible: add recipients again; alerts missed meanwhile are not re-sent.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. Working mail sending and the Email alerting feature switched on.
info.recommended: At least two addresses, ideally a monitored team mailbox, so alerts are seen even when one person is away.

settings.label: Daily digest recipients
settings.default: Blank (the digest goes to the alert recipients)

info.what: Who receives the daily summary mail sent by the scheduled daily-summary job (once every 24 hours by default; the cadence is on the Jobs page).
info.enabled: When set: the daily summary goes only to these addresses instead of the alert recipients, from the job's next run.
info.disabled: When blank: the daily summary goes to the alert recipients; if those are empty too, it is not sent.
info.risk: Low. The summary describes your privileged-access estate, so keep it to people who may see that. Reversible at any time.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. Working mail sending, the Email alerting feature on, and the daily-summary job enabled.
info.recommended: Leave blank unless the people who want the daily overview differ from those who handle alerts.

settings.label: Tier report recipients
settings.default: Blank (the tier report goes to the alert recipients)

info.what: Who receives the tier-impact report mail sent by the scheduled tier-report job (once every 24 hours by default) -- which admins hold which tier 0/1 access.
info.enabled: When set: the tier report goes only to these addresses instead of the alert recipients, from the job's next run.
info.disabled: When blank: the tier report goes to the alert recipients; if those are empty too, it is not sent.
info.risk: The report lists who holds your most privileged access, so send it only to people entitled to that view. Reversible at any time.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. Pro edition (the tier-impact report is a Pro feature). Working mail sending, the Email alerting feature on, and the tier-report job enabled.
info.recommended: Set it to your security lead or security team when they, rather than the operations team, own tier 0/1 reviews.

info.what: Which situations send an alert. Run failure: a scheduled run failed or a safety breaker held it (re-mailed at most daily). Drift: the tenant differs from the desired state (default every two weeks). Expiring access: access ending within 14 days or lifecycle dates due within 30 days. Break-glass: an emergency override was activated. Coverage: new gaps, orphan or unmanaged privileged groups, ownerless departments, unanswered reviews. Target missing: a delegation's Azure resource or role is gone (daily). Pending: changes staged over a day ago and never committed (daily).
info.enabled: When an event is on: its alert is mailed to the alert recipients and posted to the webhook, and recorded in Recent alerts. The PIM Manager applies a change at once; scheduled jobs on their next run. Run-failure alerts wait 45 minutes after a commit while it rolls out. A further event, sessions-revoked (a sign-in session revoke was queued), is listed by its raw name.
info.disabled: When an event is off: that alert is not mailed or posted. The underlying pages (Drift, Coverage, Jobs, Pending changes) still show the findings.
info.risk: Turning off engine failure or break-glass hides failed runs and emergency access from the people who should react. Safety-breaker mails (removal budget, disable abort, policy mass change) are sent to the recipients regardless of these switches. Reversible: switch the event back on; alerts skipped meanwhile are not re-sent.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. Alert recipients or a webhook, and working mail sending. The drift report cadence is a separate SuperAdmin setting on the same card.
info.recommended: Leave every event on. If one is too noisy, fix its cause or adjust that job's cadence rather than switching the event off.

info.what: An HTTPS address -- a Microsoft Teams incoming webhook or any endpoint that accepts JSON -- that receives each alert in addition to email. It works even when no mail sending is set up and is not affected by the email kill switch.
info.enabled: When set: every enabled alert raised by the PIM Manager itself (break-glass, expiring access on Home, sessions revoked, test alerts, and job failures it records) is posted with its title, details, tenant name and a link back to PIM Manager. Only https addresses on public host names are accepted; private, loopback and bare host names are rejected and the card says why.
info.disabled: When blank: alerts are delivered by email only.
info.risk: The URL is itself a credential -- anyone who has it can post into that channel -- so only Admins can see it. Alert details (account names, groups, roles) leave your environment to that endpoint. Alerts raised by the scheduled engine job are mailed but not posted to the webhook. Reversible: clear the URL and save.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. Outbound HTTPS from the PIM Manager to the endpoint. The 'Teams / webhook alerting' feature switch (Feature customization, on by default) must be on: switched off, nothing is posted even with a URL saved.
info.recommended: Use a Teams channel your operations team watches, alongside email recipients, so failures are seen even if mail stops.

info.what: The shape of what is posted to the outbound webhook. Microsoft Teams posts a message card with a colour by severity, the alert facts and an Open PIM Manager button. Generic JSON posts a flat object with event, title, detail, severity, tenant, link and time, for a Logic App or your own receiver.
info.enabled: When set to Microsoft Teams: the next alert is posted as a Teams message card.
info.disabled: At the default (Generic JSON): the next alert is posted as a flat JSON object. A Teams webhook given Generic JSON may show the raw text or reject it.
info.risk: Low. A format the endpoint does not understand makes the post fail; the failure shows in Recent alerts. Reversible at any time.
info.requires: Admin role in PIM Manager. An outbound webhook URL.
info.recommended: Microsoft Teams for a Teams incoming webhook; Generic JSON for anything else.

info.what: The longest activation PIM Manager lets any policy template allow, picked from 1 hour to 3 days. On every run the engine applies it to the activation policies it writes for the groups and roles PIM Manager manages: a template whose 'An activation lasts at most' is longer is shortened to this value. A template that is already shorter is left as it is.
info.enabled: When set lower than a template: on the next engine run the activation policies that use that template are shortened to this value in Entra, through the normal policy apply and its safety checks (a large change set is held for approval). The engine log names each template it shortened.
info.disabled: At the default (1 day): nothing changes -- Entra itself allows at most 24 hours for an activation, so the default never shortens a template.
info.risk: Medium when you lower it: people who activate for longer than the new value have to activate again sooner. Activations already running are not cut short. Reversible: pick a longer value and save; the next engine run applies the template's own value again.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. Applies only to groups and roles PIM Manager manages.
info.recommended: Leave it at 1 day and set the activation length per template; lower it to enforce a maximum across every template.

info.what: The longest eligible assignment PIM Manager lets a policy template allow (30, 90, 180 or 365 days). The engine applies it to the policies it writes for the groups and roles PIM Manager manages, where the template requires an eligibility to end: a longer maximum is shortened to this value. A template that allows a permanent eligibility keeps it.
info.enabled: When set lower than a template: on the next engine run Entra is told that new eligible assignments under that template may last at most this long. The engine log names each template it shortened.
info.disabled: At the default (365 days): nothing changes -- 365 days is also the longest the shipped templates allow.
info.risk: Medium when you lower it: new or renewed eligibilities end sooner, so people need them renewed more often. Eligibilities that exist today are not shortened. Reversible: pick a longer value and save.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. Applies only to groups and roles PIM Manager manages.
info.recommended: Leave it at 365 days unless your policy demands shorter eligibility everywhere.

info.what: A floor on every activation policy the engine writes for the groups and roles PIM Manager manages. When it is on, the engine adds MFA to the 'To activate, require' checks of any policy template that sets those checks without MFA (a template that asks for a Conditional Access authentication context counts as covered). It never removes a check a template asks for.
info.enabled: When on: on the next engine run every managed group and role whose template sets activation checks without MFA requires MFA when someone activates, through the normal policy apply and its safety checks. A template that sets no activation checks at all is reported in the engine log and left to Entra.
info.disabled: When off: the engine applies the activation checks exactly as each policy template says -- a template without MFA then activates without MFA. Turning it off does not by itself remove MFA anywhere: the shipped templates all require MFA.
info.risk: Low when on (people must complete MFA when they activate). Turning it off removes the safety net for a template that forgets MFA. Reversible at any time; the next engine run applies the new value.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. Applies only to groups and roles PIM Manager manages.
info.recommended: Keep it on.

settings.label: Workload exemptions
settings.where: Settings > Hybrid AD & workloads > Workload exemptions

info.what: A list of workload role bindings (for example a Defender XDR or Intune role for a group) that you deliberately do not want created. Each entry names a workload and/or a role, optionally a group tag and a scope, a reason, and an expiry date or No expiry. A blank group tag or scope means 'any'.
info.enabled: When an entry is active: the workload reconciliation shows the binding as 'exempted' instead of 'missing', and on its next run the engine's workload connector reports it and does not create it. It never removes a binding that already exists. The day after the expiry date the exemption stops counting, the binding shows as missing again and the next run creates it.
info.disabled: When the list is empty: every desired workload binding is expected to exist, and the engine creates any that are missing on its next run.
info.risk: An entry with only a workload (no role) excuses every role of that workload. Removing an entry, or letting it expire, lets the engine create that role assignment in your tenant on its next run. Only the generic workload connector honours exemptions; a Defender XDR row that carries its own custom role definition is applied by a separate step that does not read this list. Reversible: add or remove entries at any time.
info.requires: Admin to add or remove entries; anyone can read them. Free (Community) and Pro. Takes effect only where the workload connectors are on and the engine has the workload's own permissions.
info.recommended: Use it sparingly, always with a real reason and an expiry date, so an exemption is reviewed instead of becoming permanent.

settings.label: Keep configuration backups for (days)
settings.where: Operations > Backups & restore (also Settings > Copy & tools > Configuration backups)

info.what: How many days PIM Manager keeps its daily configuration backups (departments, external companies, admins, group definitions, delegations, workload bindings and settings -- never secrets). Any whole number from 1 to 3650.
info.enabled: When set: once a day the backup job takes a backup (or records 'no change') and then deletes every backup older than this many days. Pinned backups are always kept, the newest real backup is always kept so there is a restore point, and a backup a kept 'no change' record points to is kept. Each prune is written to the audit trail.
info.disabled: At the default (90 days): the same daily prune, with a 90-day window.
info.risk: Lowering the value deletes older backups permanently at the next daily run -- they cannot be restored afterwards. Pin any backup you must keep before you lower it. Raising it keeps more backups (more database space). Reversible for the future only: a higher value does not bring back backups already pruned.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it; Admin can read it. Free (Community) and Pro. The daily config-backup job must be enabled (it is by default).
info.recommended: Keep 90 days or more, and pin a backup before any large change you may want to roll back.

info.what: How long the audit trail keeps its rows. 0 keeps every row forever. Any other value must be 13 to 1200 months. Audit rows can never be edited, and the database itself refuses any delete that does not come from the retention job.
info.enabled: When set (13 months or more): the daily audit-retention job deletes the audit rows older than that, at most 50,000 per run (the rest on the following runs), and records each run -- cutoff, rows deleted, rows left -- as a new event in the audit trail.
info.disabled: At 0 (the default): the job runs and deletes nothing. Every audit row is kept.
info.risk: Deleted audit rows are gone for good: evidence for an investigation or a compliance review older than the window is lost. Check your own retention obligations first. Reversible for the future only: setting it back to 0 stops further deletes but does not restore deleted rows.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it; Admin can read it. Free (Community) and Pro. The daily audit-retention job must be enabled (it is by default).
info.recommended: Keep every row (0) unless a policy requires a limit; if you set one, use at least the period your auditors expect, for example 24 months or more.

settings.label: Extend ... days before a permission ends
settings.where: Reviews & controls > My people > Auto-extend policy

info.what: How many days before a time-bound assignment ends the engine renews it (1 to 90). It applies to every expiring delegation PIM manages: group memberships of admins, nested groups, Entra role, administrative-unit and Azure role assignments that are set to auto-extend.
info.enabled: When set: on each engine run, an assignment that ends within this many days and is allowed to extend is renewed for the row's number of days, counted from that run. The 'Upcoming automatic extensions' list and the monthly owner mail show the date each one will be extended. Takes effect on the next engine run.
info.disabled: At the default (14 days): assignments are renewed 14 days before they end.
info.risk: Too short a lead time leaves little room if an engine run fails, so access can lapse. A long lead time renews earlier and gives owners less time to deny. Reversible: change it; the next run uses the new value.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. The engine needs the same rights it uses to create the assignments (for example RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory).
info.recommended: Keep 14 days: enough margin for a failed run, and owners still get their monthly list to deny what should end.

settings.label: Rows without an AutoExtend value are extended
settings.where: Reviews & controls > My people > Auto-extend policy

info.what: What a blank AutoExtend cell on a delegation row means. Who decides an extension, first match wins: an access review outcome (Keep extends, Remove does not), then an owner's Deny of that exact end date, then the row's own TRUE / FALSE, and only then this default.
info.enabled: When on: a row with a blank AutoExtend value is renewed by the engine before it ends, like a row set to TRUE, unless a review or an owner says otherwise. Silence means extend.
info.disabled: When off: a row with a blank AutoExtend value is NOT renewed. On its end date the membership or role assignment simply ends in your tenant, and the person loses that access.
info.risk: Switching it off can make many people lose access on their end dates without anyone acting -- every row created without an explicit AutoExtend value is affected. Reversible: switch it back on; the next engine run renews what is still live, but an assignment that already ended is only recreated by the engine's normal reconcile of the row.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. Works together with the lead time above and with access reviews and owner decisions on the same page.
info.recommended: Keep it on, and use explicit AutoExtend=FALSE on rows (or an owner Deny) for access that must end.

info.what: Whether a change must be committed by a different administrator than the one who staged it. Off: anyone may commit what they staged. Sensitive: changes classed as sensitive (a privileged role or scope added to a group, a guest put into a privileged group, a disable or offboarding) need a second person. All: every change does.
info.enabled: When set to Sensitive or All: a commit that carries out a change you staged yourself -- or, under All, any direct edit you make -- is refused with 'a second administrator must commit this', and the refusal is audited. Another administrator opens the shared queue and commits it. Applies from the next commit.
info.disabled: When Off (the default): the person who staged a change may commit it. Rows staged by a colleague stay locked to them in every mode.
info.risk: With only one administrator, Sensitive or All blocks that person's own commits. Note that a SuperAdmin can switch the mode back to Off alone. Turning it Off removes the four-eyes check on your configuration. Reversible at any time.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. Needs at least two people with the Admin or SuperAdmin role.
info.recommended: Sensitive, when you have two or more administrators: privileged changes get a second pair of eyes without slowing everyday edits.

info.what: Whether releasing a safety guard needs a second SuperAdmin. A release lets one held engine plan through for one run or until a time (at most 24 hours) -- for example more removals than the per-run removal budget, or more account disables than the circuit breaker allows.
info.enabled: When on: a new release is created as pending. The engine will not use it until a different SuperAdmin approves it on the Guards page. The person who created it cannot approve it. If the setting cannot be read, PIM Manager treats it as on.
info.disabled: When off (the default): one SuperAdmin with a reason of at least 10 characters releases a guard alone, and the next matching engine run may use it.
info.risk: Off means a single SuperAdmin can let the engine remove or disable more than the guards normally allow in one run. The switch itself can be turned off by one SuperAdmin. Releases are always audited and bound to the exact plan; a changed plan is held again. Reversible at any time; a release already pending stays pending.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. Needs at least two SuperAdmins when on.
info.recommended: On, when you have two or more SuperAdmins: a release can remove access at scale, so it deserves a second pair of eyes.

settings.label: Break-glass accounts
settings.where: Settings > Emergency access (break-glass); also Get Started > Break-glass

info.what: The emergency accounts PIM must never lock out, by sign-in name (UPN) or object id. Both PIM Manager and the engine read this one list. A change is not applied directly: it becomes a request that a different SuperAdmin must approve within 72 hours, and every step is audited.
info.enabled: When an account is on the list: every revoke, disable, sign-in session revoke and offboarding path in PIM skips it -- the engine, queued actions, access reviews and the disable circuit breaker. From the engine's next run after the request is approved.
info.disabled: When the list is empty: no account is exempt, so PIM can revoke, disable or offboard any account its rules reach -- including your emergency accounts.
info.risk: Adding an account shields it from every PIM guard, so only list real emergency accounts. Removing one makes it reachable by PIM's removals again. If the list cannot be read, PIM treats every account as break-glass and removes nothing that run. Reversible through a new approved request.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to request a change, and a second, different SuperAdmin to approve it. Free (Community) and Pro.
info.recommended: List your two or more cloud-only emergency accounts by UPN, and keep them out of every PIM group.

settings.label: PIM Activator target groups (PROD / TEST) and additional tenants
settings.default: No group for PROD or TEST; no additional tenants

info.what: The group of admins that gets the PIM Activator browser extension, one for PROD and one for TEST, picked from your directory, plus an optional list of extra tenants for the extension's catalog. PIM Manager writes nothing to your tenant here: the values are filled into the ready-made commands on the page that an admin downloads and runs.
info.enabled: When a group is set: every command for that channel assigns that group (and only that group) to the PIM Activator app and targets it for the extension. The group is checked in your directory before it is saved. Extra tenants are validated and added to the commands' catalog.
info.disabled: When blank (the default): the commands assign nobody and say so -- nobody can sign in to the PIM Activator until you choose a group. Never all users or all devices.
info.risk: A too-broad group lets more people sign in to the PIM Activator once an admin runs the commands. Changing the group only changes the command text; groups already assigned in your tenant stay until you change them there. Reversible: pick another group or clear it.
info.requires: Admin to change it. The Manager needs to read groups in your directory to confirm the group. Running the commands needs an admin who can create app registrations and assign apps.
info.recommended: Use a dedicated group holding only your administrators, and a separate small group for TEST.

settings.label: Policy template used where a delegation names none -- PIM for Groups

info.what: The policy template the engine applies to the PIM for Groups policy of every group PIM manages whose definition leaves the policy template blank. The template sets how long an activation lasts, what is required to activate (for example MFA, justification) and whether approval is needed.
info.enabled: When set: on its next run the engine compares each such group's live member policy with the chosen template and updates the ones that differ. Only groups PIM manages are touched. Large policy changes in one run are held by the policy mass-change guard until approved.
info.disabled: At the built-in default: these groups follow Groups_Standard.
info.risk: Picking a weaker template weakens activation rules on many groups at once; picking one that requires approval makes every such activation wait for an approver. Reversible: pick the previous template; the next run puts the old rules back.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. The template must exist and be written for PIM for Groups. The engine needs RoleManagementPolicy.ReadWrite.AzureADGroup.
info.recommended: Keep the built-in default unless your organisation has its own group standard; name a template on the definitions that need stricter rules.

settings.label: Policy template used where a delegation names none -- Entra ID roles

info.what: The policy template the engine applies to the Entra ID role policy of every role your delegations assign (to groups, in administrative units, or directly) when the row leaves the policy template blank. If two rows name the same role with different templates, the one requiring approval wins.
info.enabled: When set: on its next run the engine updates each such role's PIM policy (activation length, activation checks, approval) to match the chosen template. Only roles a delegation names are touched. A large change in one run is held by the policy mass-change guard until approved.
info.disabled: At the built-in default: these roles follow EntraIDRoles_Standard.
info.risk: A role policy applies to everyone who holds that role in the tenant, not only PIM's groups. A weaker template weakens it for all of them. Reversible: pick the previous template; the next run restores the old rules.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. The template must exist and be written for Entra ID roles. The engine needs RoleManagementPolicy.ReadWrite.Directory.
info.recommended: Keep the built-in default, and name an approval-required template on the rows for your most privileged roles.

settings.label: Policy template used where a delegation names none -- Azure resource roles

info.what: The policy template the engine applies to the PIM policy of each Azure role and scope pair your Azure delegations assign when the row leaves the policy template blank. If two rows name the same pair with different templates, the one requiring approval wins.
info.enabled: When set: on its next run the engine updates the role policy on each such scope (activation length, activation checks, approval) to match the chosen template. Only role and scope pairs a delegation names are touched. Too many or too many weakening changes in one run trip the Azure policy breaker and wait for approval.
info.disabled: At the built-in default: these pairs follow AzureRoles_Standard (the same rules as the Entra role standard).
info.risk: An Azure role policy applies to everyone eligible for that role on that scope. A weaker template weakens it for all of them. Reversible: pick the previous template; the next run restores the old rules.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Free (Community) and Pro. The template must exist and be written for Azure resource roles. The engine's identity needs a role that may change role management policies on those scopes (for example User Access Administrator or Owner).
info.recommended: Keep the built-in default, and name an approval-required template on rows that grant Owner or User Access Administrator.

settings.label: Manage delegation / role mapping
settings.default: Empty (only the access granted at setup applies; every other signed-in user is a Reader)

info.what: Who may do what in PIM Manager: each sign-in name is mapped to Reader (view only), Delegated (view only, limited to the groups they own), Admin (stage, commit and revoke) or SuperAdmin (everything, including settings, emergency access and this map). Each entry is one person; groups are not expanded.
info.enabled: When saved: the server enforces the map on every request, within about 15 seconds. Saving is refused if no SuperAdmin would remain, and a new Delegated entry needs Pro. Without Pro, an existing Delegated entry acts as Reader.
info.disabled: For a person not in the map (and not granted at setup): PIM Manager still lets them in as a Reader if they can sign in, so they can view configuration and assignments but not change anything.
info.risk: Admin and SuperAdmin can change who holds privileged access in your tenant through the engine, so grant them only to people who need them. Removing someone takes effect within seconds. Reversible: edit the map again. Every save is audited.
info.requires: SuperAdmin to change it. Delegated entries need Pro; Reader, Admin and SuperAdmin are Free (Community). At least one SuperAdmin must remain.
info.recommended: Keep two SuperAdmins (so second-approver controls work), give everyday operators Admin, and limit who can sign in to PIM Manager at all with the app's user assignment.
